news.Title: Jensen Huang Resigns, Leaving CFO Colette Kress to Run Nvidia
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Nvidia Corp. ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) fell 11% in premarket after the company said co-founder Jensen Huang had resigned as president,CEO and a member of the board, effective immediately.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with NVDA.

Colette Kress, Nvidia's CFO since 2013, will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role until a permanent successor is named. Before Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance at companies including Cisco (CSCO) and Microsoft (MSFT). The board said it will consider internal and external candidates. It also appointed Harvey C. Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys, as its first-ever chair. Jones said the board expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to continue without interruption.

The change lands days before Nvidia's results for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, which the company said will be released on November 17 as scheduled. Those results will be the first under interim leadership. Huang, who led Nvidia for 33 years, owns about 3.6% of the company.

news.Title: Who is NVIDIA’s new CEO Colette Kress?
news.Content:
Investing.com -- NVIDIA has appointed longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO following the shock resignation of Jensen Huang, who led the chipmaker for 33 years.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

Kress, 59, has spent more than 13 years at NVIDIA and is regarded as one of its most influential executives, with deep knowledge of the company's operations, financial strategy and relationships with major customers.

She joined NVIDIA in September 2013, following nearly 25 years in finance roles at major technology companies, including Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.

Before NVIDIA, Kress spent three years as a senior vice president and finance chief at Cisco, overseeing financial strategy, planning and business development. She previously worked at Microsoft for 13 years, including four as CFO of its Server and Tools division.

She holds a bachelor's degree in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

During her tenure, NVIDIA transformed from a company primarily associated with gaming graphics cards into the dominant supplier of AI computing infrastructure. Its annual revenue surged from just over $4 billion in fiscal 2013 to nearly $216 billion in fiscal 2026.

Kress has also become a familiar face to Wall Street, regularly appearing alongside Huang on quarterly earnings calls, discussing financial performance, customer demand, supply constraints and the company's outlook.

Despite her CFO title, analysts say her influence has extended well beyond financial management.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

"She's more than just a CFO," Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co., told CNBC, describing her as more of a chief operating officer.

Ives called Kress a "Swiss Army knife" for NVIDIA, saying she was closely involved in strategic decisions spanning technology, customers and partnerships.

Still, succeeding Huang presents an extraordinary challenge.

Unlike Kress, Huang was an engineer and founder who remained deeply involved in product development, technology decisions and NVIDIA's long-term strategy. His management structure also left the company without a traditional second-in-command.

Story Continues

Kress acknowledged the challenge in Thursday's announcement, saying she was committed to building on the "extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years."

Newly appointed board chairman Harvey Jones expressed confidence in Kress, citing her understanding of NVIDIA's customers, operations and finances.

Her appointment is interim, with the board considering both internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO position. Kress will retain her CFO responsibilities during the transition.

The leadership shakeup comes amid mounting controversy surrounding Huang's reported extramarital affairs, including one involving a Chinese businesswoman suspected by U.S. authorities of having intelligence ties to Beijing.

The allegations prompted an independent board investigation and ultimately preceded Huang's departure. NVIDIA shares plunged more than 12% in early Thursday trading as investors assessed the implications of losing the executive most closely associated with the AI boom.

Kress now faces her first major test almost immediately, with NVIDIA scheduled to report quarterly earnings on November 17.

news.Title: Jensen Huang's exit puts Nvidia's $530 billion web of AI deals under the microscope
news.Content:
Jensen Huang didn't just sell chips for the AI boom. He helped pay for it, and Wall Street is now repricing everyone on his tab.

Huang resigned as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO and left its board Thursday, effective immediately, after reports of two affairs , one involving an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the company still plans to report earnings Tuesday.

Nvidia stock sank to its lowest level in more than a year, putting it about $2 trillion below its October record at its low. But the selling hasn't hit the AI trade evenly . Nebius ( NBIS ) and CoreWeave ( CRWV ), cloud companies that rent out Nvidia chips, took the worst of it, while rivals Broadcom ( AVGO ) and AMD ( AMD ) and most of Big Tech held up.

That pattern traces the bank of Nvidia .

Nvidia owns stakes in Intel ( INTC ), SpaceX ( SPCX ), CoreWeave, and Coherent ( COHR ), and it has pledged up to $10 billion to Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) ahead of its IPO next week . It also has a preliminary deal to put as much as $100 billion into OpenAI.

Nvidia's latest quarterly filing lists about $530 billion in commitments and guarantees, by Yahoo Finance's count, including roughly $65 billion to rent back cloud capacity from companies like CoreWeave and a guarantee of up to $105 billion on OpenAI's Ohio data center leases.

"It does bring into question what we've been talking about for ... the better part of the last year, which is a lot of these circular relationships," Liz Thomas, chief market strategist at SoFi, said at Yahoo Finance Invest .

What to know about Jensen Huang's resignation:

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid affair scandals

Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?

3 challenges for a post-Jensen Huang Nvidia

The pressure points

The first is the dealmaker himself. Huang sat at the center of these deals, and Kress, who signed off on them as CFO, now decides how many more to write.

The OpenAI guarantee pays out only if OpenAI defaults, and the kind of downturn that would sink OpenAI would likely hit Nvidia's own sales at the same time.

Customers are paying slower too. Nvidia's receivables hit $63 billion last quarter, with bills taking about 60 days to collect, up from 45. Nvidia blamed longer terms on big deals.

And its own portfolio is shrinking. The value of Nvidia's largest public stock holdings has fallen by about $24 billion since June, led by Intel.

The money behind the AI build-out was already getting harder to find. CoreWeave's CEO said this week the company won't borrow without collateral at today's high rates. BofA's Savita Subramanian told Yahoo Finance the tech giants are now selling more of their own stock than they buy back, saying they're "net issuers today rather than buying back their stock."

Story Continues

Nvidia's balance sheet is the counterweight, with about $99 billion in cash and securities against $33 billion of debt at the end of July.

Tuesday's earnings report will show whether Kress stands behind the guidance and the commitments, and whether customers are paying on time.

Thomas put the question for next week bluntly.

"Can the market survive without positive results from Nvidia?"

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) remained flat. Nvidia stock tumbled 7% after trimming losses. Follow the latest developments on Nvidia's CEO here . Some chipmakers, including Intel ( INTC ) and Micron ( MU ) fell, while others, such as Nvidia rival AMD ( AMD ) rose. news.Title: Rivian CEO says robotaxis won't end car ownership — he's betting on both
news.Content: Rivian ( RIVN ) CEO RJ Scaringe doesn't think robotaxis will kill car ownership in America — and he's building the company's self-driving strategy around that belief. "I don't think it's the end of car ownership. I think maybe it goes from 95% to 90% [of miles driven in personally owned vehicles]," Scaringe said at Yahoo Finance Invest . His view comes as the EV maker pours investment into autonomy on both the software and hardware sides. Scaringe expects driverless rides to grow fastest in dense cities like New York. But he doesn't see the whole country giving up its cars to "use rideshare services and unplug and plug in car seats." So the company is betting on both sides — unlike Tesla ( TSLA ), which seems to be betting fully on autonomous products like the Cybercab and killing off vehicles like the Model S, Model X , and Cybertruck . For Rivian, the robotaxi is on one side. The company struck a deal with Uber worth up to $1.25 billion to supply as many as 50,000 robotaxi versions of its R2 SUV. The first 10,000 are set for San Francisco and Miami by 2028. "Particularly for places like New York, San Francisco, downtown Seattle, like these more urban dense environments, it's an incredible unlock," Scaringe said. On the other side is a self-driving car for personal use. Scaringe described a Rivian that can "drive you to the airport and drive itself back home" or "go pick up the kids from school." (Scaringe, a parent to three young children, has said in the past that he would love to see that happen.) Fully self-driving cars could shrink a two- or three-car household to one or two vehicles, he said. He expects new models in between, like neighbors co-owning a car that drops one person off at work and then comes back for the other. Those will likely emerge "in the 2030s," he said. The first step is point-to-point driving, where the owner types in an address and the car drives there while the driver supervises. Rivian began inviting select Autonomy+ subscribers into an early access program on Oct. 15, with a wider rollout planned for next year. Scaringe calls it a "staircase" toward Level 4, where the car can drive itself with nobody inside. Getting there depends on how the software develops — and the company's own neural nets. Older self-driving systems relied on handwritten rules, like stay in the lane and don't hit the car ahead. That approach breaks down in complex situations. "You get to a roundabout, and suddenly it's very hard to describe how to behave in a roundabout," Scaringe said. Story Continues Rivian's Large Driving Model (LDM) — powered by a neural net — learns behavior from millions of miles of real driving. Scaringe compared it to a driver from Missouri adjusting to Manhattan: "Okay, those yellow things [cabs] are really aggressive," he joked. Because Rivian sells to consumers, its cars are everywhere, giving the company a diverse dataset for training. But that fleet is far smaller than Tesla's, and Waymo already runs driverless rides in several cities. That's where the R2 comes in to fill in the data pipeline. R2 was Rivian's bestselling vehicle in the third quarter. It helped push deliveries to a record 19,248 and revenue up 38% to $2.155 billion. Still, "mass market" is a stretch for now. The only R2 on sale is the $57,990 Launch Package , and the roughly $45,000 base model isn't due until late 2027. Smaller, cheaper R3 and R4 models will follow. Software is already paying off, however. Software and services revenue rose 45% to $605 million in the quarter , with $354 million coming from its Volkswagen joint venture. The car business still lost money, though, and Rivian expects an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.75 billion to $1.85 billion this year. Despite the spending on AI, Scaringe is no doomsayer about the technology. "AI is ultimately a tool," he said. "It's capable of doing bad things if it's directed to do bad things. But it's not a sentient being." Follow Pras Subramanian on X and Instagram . news.Title: Alphabet and Meta Platforms Pay Dividends. Is Either of Them Worth Owning for Income?
news.Content:
Both Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) instituted a notable change to their capital allocation policies in 2024. The social media giant moved first. In February of that year, it introduced a $0.50 quarterly dividend. The Google parent followed suit, announcing a quarterly payout of $0.20 in April 2024.

These companies have been wonderful to their shareholders over the years. Both have outperformed the S&P 500 index in the past decade. Capital appreciation was the main driver of returns in investment portfolios.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But now that dividends are a mainstay, do either of these "Magnificent Seven" stocks make sense for investors seeking income-generating opportunities?

Capital allocation has evolved

These companies have raised their dividends in the past couple of years. Alphabet currently pays $0.22 per share, up 10% from the initial distribution. Meta Platforms' dividend is up 5% from the beginning to $0.525 today. While the growth is certainly small, these leadership teams are at least hinting to shareholders that slowly increasing the payouts might be a permanent feature.

There is minimal risk that these dividends come under any pressure. Both businesses have historically operated from a position of financial robustness. In the past five years, Alphabet's quarterly operating margin averaged a fantastic 30.4%. At 36.4%, Meta Platforms' average margin is even better. And combined, they have $67.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents on their balance sheets.

Dividends are well covered by their earnings streams. Through the first nine months of 2026, Alphabet's net income was almost 25 times higher than its dividends, while Meta Platforms' bottom line was nearly 13 times greater than what it paid in distributions to shareholders. From this vantage point, it looks like the payouts are safe.

However, investors shouldn't rush to buy these businesses if all they're after is a meaningful income stream. The dividend yields are tiny. Alphabet, at a dividend yield of 0.31%, and Meta Platforms, at 0.33%, aren't attracting any attention in this regard. These figures are significantly lower than the inflation rate.

There are superior choices out there. The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF , for example, offers a much better dividend yield of 1.07%. More stable consumer stocks, like Coca-Cola , Procter & Gamble , and Altria Group , pay investors sizable amounts. And it's hard to ignore the 10-year Treasury, which currently yields 5%.

Story Continues

There's only one reason to own these tech stocks

Given how small their dividend yields are, Alphabet and Meta Platforms don't exactly cater to income seekers. On the other hand, they still target investors who want to add growth opportunities to their portfolios. These businesses offer the potential for market-beating returns over the next five or 10 years.

Their scale is not an inhibitor. Alphabet posted 25% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3, similar to Meta Platforms' 26% gain. This points to long expansionary runways ahead. These companies are direct beneficiaries of the internet's proliferation.

These management teams have been directing their time and resources to artificial intelligence (AI), which is sucking up capital that might otherwise have gone to raising dividend payouts. Both Alphabet and Meta Platforms will invest hundreds of billions of dollars this year in technical infrastructure to expand compute capacity and support their AI initiatives.

And they're raising external funding to power these ambitions, in turn pausing share buybacks, which historically played a key role in returning capital to investors. Free cash flow has also turned negative. This development will test the market's patience because nobody knows the kinds of returns these substantial AI-related investments will bring. It's impossible to predict when the data center spending boom will peak or who will capture the excess profits.

On an earnings basis, however, these two leading technology stocks trade at very compelling valuations. Market sentiment reflects elevated levels of uncertainty.

news.Content:
輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳因外遇風波連環爆，於台灣時間今（12）晚宣布辭去執行長及董事職務，震撼彈波及台指期夜盤一度湧現恐慌賣壓。指數盤中跌破4萬3,000點整數關卡，最低跌超過700點。不過，逢低買盤大舉進場，指數隨即展開深V強彈，低點反彈逼近千點。

黃仁勳確定下台的消息不僅影響輝達開盤，也波及台指期夜盤，恐慌性賣壓一度湧現，指數盤中跌破4萬3,000點整數關卡，最低觸及42,371點，較前一日收盤大跌757點。

不過，隨著市場逐步消化利空、逢低承接買盤大舉進場，帶動指數快速反彈。截至晚間10時57分，台指期夜盤暫報43,353點，不僅順利重返4萬3,000點大關，更由黑翻紅轉漲225點。

從盤中低點起算，高低震盪反彈高達982點、逼近千點，顯示市場多空交戰激烈、情緒劇烈擺盪。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: Qualcomm CEO: AI won't replace your smartphone anytime soon
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) has the Muse charm and AI-friendly glasses.

OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) is still testing an AI-forward hardware device.

Snap ( SNAP ) recently dropped its latest AI smart glasses.

And Tesla ( TSLA ) is starting to pump out humanoid robots.

But despite all the advancements in tech hardware, the good old smartphone will still have a starring role in our lives as AI becomes more powerful, according to Qualcomm ( QCOM ) CEO Cristiano Amon.

"There's something very interesting happening with the phone right now. In the short term, the phone market is, it's bad, right? It's suppressed because of memory prices. The market has been down in 2026, and 2027 is going to be probably flat to down. But the most important thing is that the phone is not going anywhere," Amon said at Yahoo Finance Invest.

Amon explained how AI — particularly agentic AI — will change how we use our phones. "You are going to continue to operate your phone for everything that's relevant to you, your apps, but you're going to have agents. They're going to operate the phone for you, and eventually, certain workloads, you're going to relegate to the agent," he said, adding that phones will "play a very important processing hub for a lot of the content and the sensing, even as workloads shift to glasses and other personal AI devices. So what we are seeing right now in the mobile space, a lot of traction with glasses, a lot of traction with different things like keychains for agents like the Muse, and watches are becoming interesting again, and a lot of processing on the phone. So, phone's not going to go anywhere. Workloads are going to shift, and eventually you're going to have a more powerful phone. We just need to go follow that transition."

Qualcomm remains a major player in the handset market even as it increasingly diversifies its business to auto technology and advanced AI chips.

Handset chips remained Qualcomm's single largest business in the most recent quarter . But smartphone processor revenue dropped 26% year over year to $5.14 billion in its fiscal fourth quarter due to industrywide memory shortages and Apple's ( AAPL ) transition toward in-house modems.

Insights from Yahoo Finance Invest 2026

Qualcomm CEO on tech stock meltdown: 'There is no AI correction' for us

Qualcomm CEO: Elon Musk is serious about SpaceX's cellular network ambitions

Yahoo Finance Company of the Year: Anthropic's AI dominance

Across the entire 2026 fiscal year, smartphone sales accounted for $24.07 billion of the company's $37.21 billion total semiconductor revenue. Sales for the fiscal year dropped 13% from the prior year.

That mobile contraction was partially buffered by aggressive non-handset diversification, led by automotive chip revenue surging 89% to a record $1.99 billion.

Story Continues

"It's interesting when you think about the mobile industry, there's a huge cemetery of companies. You have companies that went from hero to zero, the ones that didn't see the change. We're actually fortunate enough that we survived all of those different transitions," Amon said.

news.Title: 黃仁勳辭職股民炸鍋！網憂台股喊救命...「國安基金也擋不住」 5大熱議盤點
news.Content:
黃仁勳辭去輝達（NVIDIA）總裁、執行長及董事職務的消息，震撼全球。消息一出，網友紛紛直呼「今晚誰睡得著」、「完蛋了 台股末日」、「最近利空以各種意想不到的方式突襲我的股票」、「這波國安基金也救不了」。《Yahoo股市》盤點五大熱議一次看。

熱議一：股票該不該賣？網友憂台股

對於台股明日的表現，網友擔憂「明天台股會跌多少 QQ」、「台股明天會不會開盤鎖死」、「完蛋，前兩天沒出清持股真是錯誤...」「最近利空以各種意想不到的方式突襲我的股票」、「台股估值直接下修 嘻嘻」、「輝達概念股崩掉不是只有相關股，是整個台股一起下去」。

不過另一派網友認為仍須觀察，有人說「今天已反映了吧」、「希望明天跌完就利空出盡......」、「一堆人等著撿？」、「NVDA這個是利空出盡還是逃命波」。

熱議二：國安基金救得了台股嗎？

上周五進場「穩市」的國安基金也是討論焦點。有網友表示「國安基金明天才會真正進場的」、「拜託祥德糖漿明天一定要進場」，將穩盤期待寄託在國安基金身上。

不過，也有網友持悲觀看法，直言「國安基金也擋不住 這個比關稅戰還慘」、「這波國安基金也救不了」、「糖漿又不傻，這時不太可能進場」。

熱議三：台廠訂單、毛利率會變嗎？供應鏈前景引論戰

台灣供應鏈是否受影響，也是網友熱議的問題。有人問「台積電的單 沒了嗎？」、「未來還會不會這麼依賴台廠的供應鏈真的有很大的變數了...」、「老黃很挺供應鏈 給你漲 換人搞不好砍你單」、「就算訂單給台廠做，也沒之前那個甜甜價可以獲利了」、「臺廠毛利率要跌多少QQ」、「可以預期科技業準備重回毛3到4的年代」。

不過也有人提出相反看法，認為「台廠以後不用給友情價格 毛利看漲」、「不是朋友，下台是有差？」、「他是用商人角度對台廠供應鏈」。

熱議四：北士科還蓋嗎？在台投資走向受關注

輝達在台投資是否延續，尤其北士科布局，也牽動網友情緒。網友問「北士科呢」、「北士科還要蓋嗎」、「我比較好奇輝達的北市科總部會不會喊卡..」、「那臺灣總部還要蓋嗎…」、「下一步總部計劃暫緩嗎」。

另有網友憂慮「黃指定的投資案都會有變數」、「這影響真的大，以後再也不會有他來台灣跟各大老闆聚餐談投資了」。過去受到關注的「兆元宴」也被提起，有人說「這下要回顧誰參加兆元宴了..」「兆元宴變成鴻門宴了」。

熱議五：沒有黃仁勳，AI需求還在嗎？

對於人事異動是否衝擊AI產業，有網友擔心「nvda不穩，整個AI資金盤都會鬆動」、「無限永動機掰了 AI資金要斷了？」另有人認為「沒有老黃的輝達，已經沒有靈魂了，不值得投資了」，反映對創辦人離開後公司前景的疑慮。

同時也有網友指出「他只是 GPU 供應商又不是需求端」「所以他辭職就沒有AI需求了？」、「AI哪會完蛋 還有其他巨頭在推的」、「資金做輪動 AI不可能死 只不過NV投資人短期不好過了」。

至於財務長科萊特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）暫代執行長，有人表示「財務長帶領ai巨頭 XD」、「財務長就只是暫代 因為目前是空窗期」，並表示「財務長對公司治理與媒體應對是最有經驗的」。

馮萱榕／財經特派記者，主跑財政部、電腦通路、觀光餐飲等

news.Title: Apple supplier Foxconn posts record profit, raises outlook
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Foxconn, a key Apple supplier, reported record third-quarter profit on Thursday and raised its full-year outlook for all four of its main business segments, driven by strong demand for AI servers.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

Net profit rose 34% year over year to 77.5 billion New Taiwan dollars, about 10% above both Citi's and Street estimates.

Revenue jumped 46% to 3.02 trillion New Taiwan dollars, while operating profit surged 64% to 115.4 billion New Taiwan dollars. EPS rose to 5.51 New Taiwan dollars from 4.15 a year earlier.

Cloud and networking products, boosted by AI servers, made up 54% of quarterly revenue, becoming the group's largest business. Chairman Young Liu said AI servers have become Foxconn's most significant growth engine.

For the fourth quarter, Foxconn expects strong growth both sequentially and from a year earlier, helped by shipments of a new generation of AI server racks and the peak season for consumer electronics such as smartphones.

However, computing product segment "continues to be affected by tight memory supply, leading a likely slight decline quarter-over-quarter."

Foxconn also expressed optimism about 2027, though it warned that shortages of chips, memory and other key components are expected to persist, with demand continuing to exceed supply next year.

Citi reiterated its Buy rating after the results.

"Despite recent AI deployment concern, management sees strong growth outlook into 4Q26 and 2027 and expects further profitability improvement," the bank wrote.

Citi added that Foxconn has gained market share in the latest generation of AI racks and expects shipments to rise by a high-double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter. It also sees growing work on custom AI chips for cloud providers as a way to diversify Foxconn's AI revenue.

news.Title: Jim Cramer Is Bullish on These 5 Stocks Amid Nvidia Controversy
news.Content:
After years of unconditionally backing Jensen Huang and Nvidia (NASDAQ), Jim Cramer's confidence in the chipmaker has been shaken by the controversy surrounding its chief executive. And the reasons are understandable.

Cramer's investment thesis on Nvidia has always been closely tied to Huang's leadership. The CNBC host has repeatedly praised Huang as a visionary capable of transforming entire industries through artificial intelligence. He believed so strongly in Nvidia that he even named his dog after the company in 2017.

But with Huang's future now uncertain following allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy, Cramer's longtime conviction is facing a serious test. The controversy has raised questions about Huang's reputation and whether he can continue leading the company.

Cramer recently downgraded Nvidia from a buy to a hold, citing uncertainty surrounding the investigation.

Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont both trimmed their Nvidia stakes in the second quarter, even before this controversy began. See which AI stocks they still own .

That doesn't mean Cramer has turned bearish on the entire stock market (see what Cramer was buying last week ).

While the Nvidia controversy and concerns about massive AI infrastructure spending have made him increasingly cautious, Cramer believes there are still plenty of attractive investment opportunities elsewhere.

During the recent CNBC Investing Club's annual meeting, Cramer and portfolio director Jeff Marks reviewed over 30 stocks in the Club's portfolio, identifying several companies they remain bullish on. Cramer has also continued to highlight investment opportunities outside the increasingly volatile AI trade.

Against this backdrop, we take a look at 10 stocks Jim Cramer is bullish on, ranked by the number of hedge funds holding stakes in them at the end of the second quarter of 2026.

Before this controversy, two well-known billionaires were backing Nvidia as an AI stock. See who they are .

You can click to read our full list on Jim Cramer Is Bullish on These 10 Stocks Amid Nvidia Controversy . The top 5 stocks from that list are mentioned below.

Methodology

To pick the stocks, we went through CNBC's coverage of Jim Cramer's latest stock picks, mainly the reports on his CNBC Investing Club annual meeting. From that coverage, we selected 5 stocks that Cramer is bullish on. We then ranked them by the number of hedge funds holding stakes in each one at the end of the second quarter of 2026, using Insider Monkey's database of 1,000+ hedge funds.

Story Continues

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

You can see the top 5 stocks Jim Cramer is bullish on these days in our video by clicking the image below.

#5. Wells Fargo & Company (NYSE:WFC)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 94

Wells Fargo & Company (NYSE:WFC) is another banking stock Cramer remains optimistic about. In the Nov. 6 CNBC Investing Club review, Cramer and his team highlighted the removal of Wells Fargo's asset cap as an important development for the bank's long-term growth prospects.

The Club praised CEO Charlie Scharf for improving operations and investing in businesses that generate fee-based revenue, including investment banking.

Cramer's team also considered Wells Fargo shares attractively valued and expressed optimism about the company's prospects heading into 2027.

Although the Investing Club did not issue an immediate buy recommendation, its commentary reflected a positive long-term view of the bank's transformation and earnings potential. Goldman Sachs added Wells Fargo to its US Conviction List in July and said the bank is moving from defense to offense. Read Goldman's view here .

#4. Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 99

Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) is one of the enterprise software companies Jim Cramer continues to favor despite growing investor concerns about AI potentially disrupting traditional software businesses.

During the Nov. 6 portfolio review, Cramer and his team expressed confidence in Salesforce's strategy of working with leading artificial intelligence developers.

It's not clear how long Cramer can stay bullish on Salesforce (NYSE:CRM). The AI onslaught is taking a direct jab at Salesforce's business. Microsoft and Alphabet are a growing threat because they spend far more on research and development and run their own clouds. Smaller players such as Palantir and HubSpot are also growing faster than Salesforce. Over the past five years, Salesforce's share of the CRM software market has dropped to 20% from 24%.

Salesforce's profit margins also face pressure because the company does not own a cloud. It rents computing power from Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. Salesforce is moving from charging per user seat to charging for AI usage. As that happens, it will pay more to these cloud providers, which could push its gross margin lower. The same cloud giants also compete with Salesforce, so it has little room to raise prices.

Antipodes Global Fund said in its third-quarter 2026 investor letter that the growth of Agentforce, Salesforce's AI agent platform, is strengthening the company's AI story. Check the full letter here .

#3. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 169

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) remains one of Jim Cramer's favored long-term investments, even as concerns about artificial intelligence spending have unsettled parts of the technology sector.

During the Nov. 6 CNBC Investing Club review, Cramer and his team reiterated their conviction in Apple as a stock investors should hold for the long term rather than attempt to trade around short-term market fluctuations.

The Club said Apple enjoys a notable advantage in the AI race because it can incorporate technology developed by partners such as Alphabet into its products without committing the same enormous sums to building data centers.

What Cramer is saying actually forms the basis of Apple's bull case. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) has found a low-cost way to compete in AI. It partnered with Alphabet to use the Gemini model to power its new Siri, so it does not need to build massive data centers of its own. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta are spending huge sums on AI infrastructure every year, while Apple keeps its spending low and protects its cash.

The new Siri also makes the iPhone harder to leave. It pulls details from users' messages, emails and photos to give more personal answers. The longer people use it, the more it learns about them, and switching to another phone would mean losing that history. Apple also has a new way to make money from AI. Basic AI features are free today, but management has confirmed that paid tiers are coming.

Billionaire Ken Fisher shares Cramer's long-term view on Apple. Find out if you should buy the stock .

#2. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 273

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) remains one of Jim Cramer's preferred technology stocks as investors increasingly scrutinize the enormous sums being spent on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

In the Nov. 6 CNBC Investing Club portfolio review, Cramer and his team praised Microsoft's financial discipline and its ability to maintain positive free cash flow despite substantial investment in AI and cloud computing.

Cramer believes a slowdown in data center development could benefit Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ) by reducing construction costs and easing pressure on capital spending.

Microsoft already operates extensive data center infrastructure, giving it an advantage over smaller competitors that depend on new construction to expand their businesses.

A slower pace of development could also reduce pressure on capital spending and improve free cash flow, strengthening Microsoft's position amid growing concerns about the sustainability of massive AI investments.

Cramer's bullish view centers on Microsoft's ability to continue benefiting from AI adoption while maintaining a financially resilient business. Microsoft is also a top AI pick of billionaire Ken Fisher, even though the stock barely moved over the past year. Click to read our full analysis .

#1. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 369

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) is one of Jim Cramer's latest explicit stock recommendations amid concerns about slowing data center development.

In a Nov. 9 CNBC commentary, Cramer said a slowdown in the construction of new data centers could actually benefit established cloud computing companies such as Amazon and Microsoft.

Why? Cramer believes companies with extensive existing infrastructure would be better positioned than smaller competitors whose growth depends on continued construction and financing.

Cramer specifically recommended Amazon shares and discussed the possibility of the stock reaching $300, representing nearly 10% upside from its trading level at the time.

The bullish recommendation followed the CNBC Investing Club's Nov. 6 portfolio review, in which Cramer and Marks expressed confidence in Amazon's latest quarterly performance. Amazon is also one of the four stocks that both President Trump and Nancy Pelosi bought. See the other three picks .

Before its latest earnings report, Amazon was the top AI stock pick shared by Cramer and billionaire Ken Fisher. Read our full take on the stock .

While we acknowledge the potential of AMZN as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: 黃仁勳震撼請辭輝達   台指期夜盤巨幅震盪
news.Content:
AI晶片龍頭輝達（NVIDIA）於美國時間12日投下人事震撼彈，創辦人黃仁勳宣布辭去總裁、執行長及董事會成員職務，且即刻生效。消息傳出後，輝達(NVDA.O)盤前暴跌11%，台指期夜盤開盤43,180，一度漲至43,532，目前報42,436，下跌692，跌幅-1.6%。至截稿前，台指期夜盤又翻紅，報43,203，上漲75，漲幅0.17%。

AI晶片龍頭輝達（NVIDIA）於美國時間12日投下人事震撼彈，創辦人黃仁勳宣布辭去總裁、執行長及董事會成員職務，且即刻生效。輝達董事會同步宣布，由現任執行副總裁暨財務長克雷斯（Colette Kress）接任臨時執行長，並任命董事瓊斯（Harvey C. Jones）擔任公司史上首任董事會主席，正式啟動接班布局。

消息傳出後，輝達(NVDA.O)盤前暴跌11%，英特爾(INTC.O)下跌3.7%，邁威爾科技(MRVL.O)下跌5.2%，美光科技(MU.O)下跌5.2%，Arm(ARM.O)下跌4.1%，SK海力士(SKHY.O)美股下跌5.1%，台積電ADE(TSM.N)下跌3.5%。

台指期夜盤開盤43,180，一度漲至43,532，目前報42,436，下跌692，跌幅-1.6%。至截稿前，台指期夜盤又翻紅，報43,203，上漲75，漲幅0.17%。

美股期貨週四（12日）走低，黃仁勳辭職後，那斯達克100期貨下跌1.2%，標普500期貨下跌0.6%，道瓊期貨下跌47點，跌幅0.1%，博通（Broadcom）與超微（AMD）股價在盤前交易各上漲約3%，輝達股價最新下跌約13%。

隨著黃仁勳卸下長達33年的掌舵重任，輝達即將迎來後黃仁勳時代的首場公開考驗。輝達將於美西時間11月17日下午1點20分如期公布2027會計年度第3季財報，並於下午2點召開法說會，屆時臨時執行長克雷斯與經營團隊對未來營運與AI市場的最新展望，將成為全球科技業與供應鏈關注的焦點。

news.Title: Bitdeer: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Bitdeer (NASDAQ:BTDR) announced an 89% year-over-year revenue increase to $320.7 million as it transitions power assets into high-performance computing data centers. The company is pivoting from volatile Bitcoin mining to long-term contracted artificial intelligence (AI) cloud infrastructure. Three things management said stand out.

1. Contracted AI Revenue Reaches $7.6 Billion

Bitdeer is securing multiyear contracts for its high-performance computing (HPC, data centers built for intensive AI tasks) infrastructure and cloud services, giving the business visible cash flows that don't depend on cryptocurrency price swings.

Our AI platform now represents approximately $7.6 billion of expected contracted revenue.

-- Haris Basit, Chief Strategy Officer

2. Project Financing Prioritizes Non-Dilutive Capital Growth

Management is backing data center construction with asset-level debt and customer prepayments that cover more than 50% of graphics processing unit (GPU) costs, keeping share dilution low.

We prioritize non-dilutive project level financing wherever contracted cash flows can support it.

-- Michael Potter, Chief Financial Officer

3. Power Capacity Flexible Across Mining and Cloud Computing

With 3.1 gigawatts of total power capacity, Bitdeer monetizes available electricity through Bitcoin mining while preparing sites for long-term data center leases.

We can mine to monetize available power today while we develop infrastructure for long-term HPC leases, and we can invest in GPU capacity when and where we see attractive contracted demand.

Looking Ahead

Demand for artificial intelligence compute outpaces the available power supply, and Bitdeer relies on pre-energized sites, low-cost power, and proprietary hardware to convert mining locations into data centers, while maintaining financing execution and capital discipline.

Our model is built for this environment. Our AI and crypto platforms share one power foundation and complement each other.

The company aims to maximize returns by deploying power where economic value is highest, balancing short-term crypto earnings with long-term data center revenue.

Our objective is simple. Maximize the return on every power asset and protect the balance sheet while we do it.

news.Title: Warby Parker bets on Google AI glasses for growth, but privacy fears still loom
news.Content:
By Danielle Kaye

NEW YORK, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Warby Parker is entering the smart glasses market in partnership with Google and Samsung, betting that demand for the artificial intelligence wearables will balloon in the coming years.

But the New York-based fashion brand, known for its affordable eyewear, is also seeking to ‌head off privacy concerns that have weighed on existing producers of the glasses, most of which embed small cameras allowing wearers to record their ‌surroundings without taking out their phone.

The Warby Parker glasses are broadly similar to Meta smart glasses already available from Ray-Ban and Oakley maker EssilorLuxottica, which have faced regulatory scrutiny from Norway to Australia. Also ​like the Meta glasses, they will connect to an AI assistant, in this case Google's Gemini, for everything from directions to language translation.

The big difference from existing versions on the market is the privacy framework embedded in the glasses from the outset, Warby Parker Co-CEO Neil Blumenthal told Reuters.

Alphabet's Google will not use visuals captured with the glasses to train its AI. The glasses will bar facial recognition of bystanders. And a small white notification light on the front of the glasses automatically turns on when a user ‌starts recording video.

Shoppers will start placing pre-orders from Warby Parker on ⁠Thursday. Ray-Ban's Meta glasses still dominate, representing 81.3% of AI glasses shipments in the first half of this year, according to tech research group Omdia.

But brands from Warby Parker to luxury group Kering — poised to release glasses also in partnership with Google — ⁠are looking to gain a foothold. Global AI glasses shipments more than doubled in the first half of 2026 from a year ago, though growth has slowed since the second half of last year, Omdia data shows.

Meta's AI glasses also include a camera notification light on the front, a Meta spokesperson said, adding that input from safety experts helped inform the privacy features ​on ​its glasses.

CATEGORY CONFRONTS PRIVACY RISKS

Optimism that Warby Parker's "intelligent eyewear" plan will prove to be a ​major growth engine has helped its shares rally by nearly 40% this year, ‌outperforming a 10% gain in the S&P 500.

The company expects an addition of several percentage points to fourth-quarter revenue growth from the new wearable technology, executives said on an earnings call earlier this month.

"As long as the tools provide utility to customers, then we'll be successful," Blumenthal said.

Story Continues

While the core optical backdrop remains soft, smart glasses are poised to be an "increasingly important driver" of Warby Parker's growth outlook, analysts at TD Cowen wrote in a research note last week.

Still, concerns about privacy could slow their pace of growth. One of Britain's biggest pub chains has restricted the use of the frames, Norway's government is planning a temporary ban on the ‌use of AI glasses in certain locations, and Australia is considering barring the use of camera-equipped ​smart glasses in government workplaces.

GOOGLE AIMS TO REBUILD TRUST

Juston Payne, who leads extended reality products at ​Google, acknowledged that public skepticism could be a risk to growth.

"This is ​an area where, understandably, trust was lost," he told Reuters at a demo for the Warby Parker glasses in New York.

Google says ‌it will embed extensive privacy guardrails into the devices to ​prevent tampering with the recording indicator light; redact ​people's faces from video footage before it is sent to Gemini; and ban targeted advertising on the glasses.

"We are going to change this conversation," Payne said. "We are trying to raise the bar."

But it remains to be seen whether those measures will ease concern about widespread surveillance, if the glasses become ​ubiquitous.

"I'm certainly happy to hear that (video footage is) not automatically fed ‌into AI systems for training," said Calli Schroeder, who leads the AI and human rights program at the Electronic Privacy Information Center, an ​advocacy group. "But that still leaves open: a stranger has footage of my kid on their phone. That's concerning no matter how you phrase ​it."

(Reporting by Danielle Kaye in New York; Editing by Christian Plumb and Matthew Lewis)

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures sink as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns, stock tanks
news.Content: US stock futures dropped in premarket trading on Thursday after chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ) announced CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, dragging down tech stocks. Futures on the S&P 500 ( ES=F ) fell 0.3%, while contracts for the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 ( NQ=F ) dropped 1.2%, backsliding from Wednesday's chip stock-led rally. Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( YM=F ) remained in the green. Nvidia stock tumbled more than 10% in premarket trading. The chipmaker has long stood at the heart of the AI investment boom that has powered this year's stock market. Nvidia's web of tie-ups with other AI companies also creates uncertainty about how great the fallout from Huang's affairs and potential dismissal could be for the market broadly. Follow the latest developments on Nvidia's CEO here . Some chipmakers, including Intel ( INTC ) and Micron ( MU ) fell, while others, such as Nvidia rival AMD ( AMD ) rose. In Asia, stocks held steady. The tumult, which is just the latest incident to raise investor doubts about the artificial intelligence trade that has powered this year's stock market, adds even more pressure for everything to go right in Anthropic's planned public debut next week . While the bond market was closed Wednesday, Wall Street analysts have rapidly adjusted their forecasts for more and bigger interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve following Tuesday's hotter-than-expected inflation report. Most digital assets were in the red early Wednesday, with bitcoin ( BTC ) tumbling overnight. news.Title: Silicon Motion Vs. Qualcomm: Which Chipmaker Has More Potential?
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO and Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM are premier semiconductor firms with exposure to smartphones, automotive electronics and AI-driven technologies. Silicon Motion is a leading developer of microcontroller ICs for NAND flash storage devices. The semiconductor firm also designs, develops and markets high-performance, low-power semiconductor solutions for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and other customers.

Qualcomm offers high-performance, low-power chip designs for mobile devices, PCs, XR (Extended Reality), automotive, wearable, robotics, connectivity and AI use cases. The company boasts a comprehensive intellectual property portfolio comprising 4G, 5G and other technologies. Qualcomm's brands include Snapdragon systems-on-chip, FastConnect Wi-Fi and Bluetooth systems, and Qualcomm-branded 4G, 5G and IOT equipment. The company is currently integrating on-device generative AI into all of its product lines.

Let us delve a little deeper into the companies' competitive dynamics to understand which of the two is relatively better placed in the industry.

The Case for SIMO

Silicon Motion has established itself as the leading merchant supplier of client SSD (solid state drive) controllers to module makers, including most market leaders in the United States, Taiwan and China. The company believes that it is well-equipped to adapt to industry changes as it has collaborated with flash vendors to develop proprietary controller technology to overcome the existing weakness of 3D NAND and outshine peers. Silicon Motion has commenced initial sales of 3D SSD controllers to flash partners. It expects this controller to be a significant SSD controller growth driver for the next year, as NAND Flash partners' 3D capacity expands.

Silicon Motion operates a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while outsourcing manufacturing to foundries like TSMC. Consequently, the company has a low capital investment requirement as it does not need expensive fabrication plants, enabling it to adopt advanced manufacturing nodes quickly, leading to higher margins compared to integrated manufacturers. This allows the company to focus on innovation and product development rather than manufacturing complexity. The key growth drivers for SIMO include AI and high-performance computing, cloud data centers, automotive storage, smartphones and mobile devices. Each of these end markets is growing fast and offers lucrative growth potential. Over the past 10 years, the company has shipped more than 5 billion controllers cumulatively – more than any other company in the world. Silicon Motion ships more than 750 million NAND controllers on average every year.

However, sluggishness in the global economy is likely to weigh on the company's wireless and broader semiconductor market. The demand for PCs and smartphones in the end market continues to be soft as numerous suppliers are focusing on reducing their inventory levels. The near-term price fluctuation in the PC market remains a concern. Silicon Motion continues to acquire a large number of companies. While this improves revenue opportunities, business mix and profitability, it adds to integration risks. Moreover, the semiconductor industry is highly dynamic as it is prone to swift technological changes, stiff competition from evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.

Story Continues

The Case for QCOM

Qualcomm is well-positioned to meet its long-term revenue targets, driven by solid 5G traction, greater visibility and a diversified revenue stream. The company is increasingly focusing on the seamless transition from a wireless communications firm for the mobile industry to a connected processor company for the intelligent edge. Qualcomm is witnessing healthy traction in edge networking, which helps transform connectivity in cars, business enterprises, homes, smart factories, next-generation PCs, wearables and tablets. The automotive telematics and connectivity platforms, digital cockpit and C-V2X solutions are also fueling emerging automotive industry trends such as the growth of connected vehicles, the transformation of the in-car experience and vehicle electrification.

The company is aiming to extend its Oryon CPU and AI acceleration beyond smartphones into PCs and servers. Management observed that its 2026 Snapdragon X2 PC platforms are in production and positioned to enable always-on agentic experiences, supported by a Hexagon NPU delivering up to 85 TOPS. Qualcomm is entering the custom silicon space with a leading hyperscaler and expects initial shipments in the December quarter, adding a revenue stream that is not tied to handset unit cycles. The Alphawave buyout has added high-speed wired connectivity IP and custom silicon capabilities to help accelerate the company's expansion into data centers.

Despite efforts to ramp up its AI initiatives, Qualcomm has been facing tough competition from ASML Holding N.V. ASML in the AI PC market. A shift in the share among OEMs at the premium tier has reduced Qualcomm's near-term opportunity to sell integrated chipsets from the Snapdragon platform. Memory supply constraints and related pricing are adversely impacting its handset revenues as OEMs (particularly in China) continue to draw down channel inventory.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for SIMO & QCOM?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Silicon Motion's 2026 sales indicates a year-over-year rise of 120.9%, while that for EPS suggests growth of 278.9%. The EPS estimates have been trending northward (up 20.5%) over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Qualcomm's fiscal 2027 sales implies year-over-year growth of 4.4%, while that of EPS suggests a decline of 5.7%. The EPS estimates have trended down 0.9% over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of SIMO & QCOM

Over the past year, Silicon Motion has soared 112.1% compared with the industry's growth of 79.2%. Qualcomm is up 0.5% over the same period.

Qualcomm looks significantly more expensive than Silicon Motion from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, SIMO's shares currently trade at 2.33 forward sales, lower than Qualcomm's 4.12.

SIMO or QCOM: Which is a Better Pick?

Silicon Motion and Qualcomm carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Both Silicon Motion and Qualcomm expect sales and earnings to increase in the current fiscal year. In terms of price performance, SIMO has outperformed Qualcomm. SIMO has exhibited better estimate revisions than QCOM and is trading at a relative discount. With favorable metrics, Silicon Motion seems to hold a competitive edge over Qualcomm and is therefore a better investment option at the moment.

news.Title: 台股暴跌1165點！外資僅賣6.85億　專家揭「多軍互打」真相
news.Content:
台股今（12）日上演驚心動魄的震盪走低戲碼，終場重挫1,165.28點，收在43,091.87點，跌幅達2.63%，成交金額爆出新台幣1兆132.93億元天量。正當市場以為外資又在大舉提款時，盤後籌碼卻跌破眾人眼鏡：外資今日竟然只小賣6.85億元，三大法人合計甚至反手買超51.6億元！對此， 財經專家葉育碩 在臉書發文直指真相，大盤重挫並不是空軍火力太猛，而是前幾天搶反彈的 「多軍內部自己打起來了」！

【外資僅賣6.85億！三大法人反手買超51.6億元】

攤開今日證交所公布的三大法人籌碼動向，集中市場外資及陸資僅賣超6.85億元，投信更是大力扛起護盤大旗，單日豪邁買超123.85億元，自營商則賣超65.41億元，三大法人合計反倒買超51.6億元。權王台積電（2330）今日受賣壓影響下跌55元，收在2,340元。

葉育碩點出，從現貨到期貨來看，外資不僅沒有像前幾天那樣瘋狂提款，台指期未平倉空單還單日回補了4,698口，水位降至99,573口。回顧外資連續11個交易日的賣超紀錄，從10月29日至11月12日累計賣超約8,312.82億元， 但近兩日賣超金額已大幅縮減至7.66億元與6.85億元，明顯呈現「越賣越少」的跡象。

【黃仁勳換帥傳聞突襲 華爾街挑美股收盤後發難】

既然外資站在旁邊沒怎麼賣，為何台股還會爆出逾兆元成交量、重挫超過千點？葉育碩分析，導火線正是市場熟知的「Jensen（黃仁勳）恐懼事件」。就在美股收盤之後，外媒突然拋出輝達（NVDA）董事會可能撤換執行長黃仁勳的震撼彈，拖累輝達盤後股價一度急殺超過8%。

葉育碩直言，黃仁勳是整個AI產業的核心靈魂，一旦領導層傳出變數，台灣相關AI供應鏈自然難以置身事外。他更點破華爾街空軍的操作手法相當狠辣，「前天不發、昨天不發、美股盤中不發，偏偏挑在美股收盤後才發」，瞬間替原本就脆弱的AI市場投下恐慌情緒。

【不是空軍太猛！專家揭真相：多軍自己人互相開火】

面對今日「外資沒大賣、指數卻暴跌」的詭異盤勢，葉育碩用戰場作比喻，直言原本大家以為是空軍大舉攻進來，結果打開戰場一看，「怎麼全都是自己人在互相開火？」

他指出，台股前幾個交易日才剛經歷強勁反彈，許多急著進場搶反彈的短線資金，一遇到輝達換帥利空突襲，部分選擇認賠停損、部分則急著獲利了結，這才引爆了多殺多的連鎖賣壓。換言之，今日的千點長黑並非外資落跑，而是內資與多軍陣營內部出現踩踏所致。

news.Title: Factbox-Who is Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress?
news.Content:
Nov 12 (Reuters) - Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress is set to take over as interim CEO from Jensen Huang, the company said on Thursday, putting her in charge ‌of the chipmaker whose processors power the world's most advanced supercomputers and AI data ‌centers.

The appointment comes after the board ousted co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of two extramarital affairs, one with ​a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Here are five facts about Kress:

CFO SINCE 2013

Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. She has appeared alongside Jensen Huang on the company's quarterly earnings calls.

Nvidia's revenue was $4.13 billion in the ‌fiscal year she joined and $215.9 ⁠billion in fiscal 2026.

CAREER BEFORE NVIDIA

Before Nvidia, Kress spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments, then worked at Microsoft from 1997 to 2010. At ⁠Microsoft, she became chief financial officer of the Server and Tools division in 2006, with responsibility for its financial strategy, planning and reporting.

She moved to Cisco in 2010 as senior vice president and chief financial ​officer ​of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization, where ​she was responsible for financial strategy and ‌business development. She left for Nvidia in 2013.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Kress holds a bachelor of science degree in finance from the University of Arizona and a master of business administration degree from Southern Methodist University, according to Nvidia's annual report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

She joined Nvidia after nearly 25 years in finance roles at major technology companies, Fortune reported in 2024. She ‌told Fortune Nvidia was the smallest company she had ​worked for when she started there in 2013.

CONTRACT TERMS

Executive officers ​at Nvidia are employed at will and ​have no individual employment, severance or change-in-control agreements, according to the company's ‌proxy statement. Nvidia has said in earlier filings ​that many of its ​peer companies offer such agreements.

Regulatory filings show Kress' pay includes restricted stock units, including a March 2026 award that vests over four years.

WEALTH

Forbes ranks Kress No. 32 on its 2026 ​list of America's richest self-made ‌women. Her shares in the chip firm were valued at roughly $750 million, as of ​Wednesday's close, down from more than $1 billion at the stock's peak last month.

(Reporting by ​Akash Sriram in Bengaluru; Editing by Pooja Desai)

news.Title: Can HPE Sustain Growth Amid Evolving AI Market Dynamics?
news.Content:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE has been a key beneficiary of rising artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending, as hyperscalers and leading technology companies continue to ramp up investments in AI capabilities. However, the growing concentration of AI investments among a handful of hyperscalers and infrastructure providers has raised concerns about the distribution of growth opportunities across the industry.

Against this backdrop, the November 2026 sell-off in AI and semiconductor stocks has heightened investor concerns, raising the question: Can HPE sustain growth amid evolving AI market dynamics? HPE's strongest defense against the AI market correction is its diversified infrastructure portfolio, which allows it to capture spending across multiple technology categories rather than depending exclusively on demand for AI servers.

HPE's diversified portfolio spanning networking, traditional servers, storage, hybrid cloud, GreenLake and financial services could help cushion weakness in AI-related spending. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Cloud & AI revenues reached $9 billion, up 25% year over year, with a 17% operating margin. Server revenues rose 35%, while traditional server orders increased 75% as customers favored AI-ready configurations and higher-value systems.

The Juniper acquisition is broadening HPE's reach across campus and branch, data center switching, routing and security, while integration remains ahead of schedule. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Networking revenues were $2.9 billion, up 10% on a normalized basis, and operating margin was 22%. Normalized orders rose 36%, with data center switching and routing orders up high double digits and campus and branch orders up low teens.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, GreenLake customers increased 18% year over year to 52,000 from 44,000, while management cited higher net retention as customers broadened usage of software and intelligent cloud services. The platform is reinforced by Morpheus for multi-cloud orchestration and OpsRamp for monitoring and observability. Given these factors, HPE's diversified portfolio, expanding networking business and growing GreenLake adoption provide multiple growth drivers beyond AI servers. However, sustained growth will depend on execution, demand resilience and profitability.

How Competitors Fare Against HPE

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's closest competitors in this domain are Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO. Dell AI Factory combined with NVIDIA is arguably the most direct alternative for HPE private cloud AI.

Story Continues

Dell provides pre-integrated GPU servers, storage, networking and software for enterprise AI and competes head-to-head with HPE for Fortune 1000 AI deployments. Cisco focuses on AI networking and integrated AI Pods. Cisco has started competing strongly with HPE after acquiring Splunk and through its partnership with NVIDIA.

news.Title: Wall Street Analysts Believe ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON) Could Rally 29.15%: Here's is How to Trade
news.Content:
ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON) closed the last trading session at $73.62, gaining 0.4% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $95.08 indicates a 29.2% upside potential.

The mean estimate comprises 26 short-term price targets with a standard deviation of $15.96. While the lowest estimate of $68.00 indicates a 7.6% decline from the current price level, the most optimistic analyst expects the stock to surge 69.8% to reach $125.00. It's very important to note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.

But, for ON, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

Story Continues

That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

Here's Why There Could be Plenty of Upside Left in ON

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. That's because empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 2.2% over the past month, as 11 estimates have gone higher compared to no negative revision.

Moreover, ON currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much ON could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

news.Title: Will Content Capex Weigh on Netflix's Free Cash Flow Trajectory?
news.Content:
Netflix 's NFLX elevated content investment is drawing fresh attention to its free cash flow trajectory. In the third quarter of 2026, cash additions to content assets totaled $5.16 billion against content amortization of $4.24 billion, a ratio of about 1.22x. For the first nine months, cash content spend reached $14.93 billion versus amortization of $12.77 billion, or roughly 1.17x, running above the company's full-year expectation of about 1.1x.

Despite the heavier outlay, cash conversion held up. Operating cash flow rose to $3.2 billion from $2.8 billion a year ago, while free cash flow increased 8% to $2.88 billion. Year-to-date free cash flow stands at about $9.5 billion, aided by a strong $5.09 billion in the first quarter, though the second quarter was softer at $1.53 billion. Purchases of property and equipment remained modest at $279 million in the third quarter.

Guidance, however, points to a more measured path. Netflix trimmed its 2026 free cash flow outlook to about $12 billion from $12.5 billion, citing primarily the expected fourth-quarter closing of a real estate transaction, which implies roughly $2.5 billion of fourth-quarter free cash flow. The company expects fourth-quarter revenues of $13.4 billion and a 26% operating margin, including a 120-basis-point hit from headcount reductions, while guiding full-year revenues of $51.1 billion and a 31.5% operating margin. Streaming content obligations climbed to $25.2 billion from $24 billion at 2025-end.

The holiday pipeline is cash-intensive but revenue-supportive. The fourth-quarter slate includes the NFL's Thanksgiving Eve game, a Christmas Day NFL doubleheader, the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua bout, The Diplomat Season 4, Lupin: Part 4 , the final season of Emily in Paris and the film The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth . While front-loaded spending may cap near-term free cash flow expansion, live events and tentpole releases could support engagement and monetization, keeping the longer-term trajectory intact.

How Netflix's Streaming Rivals Balance Spending and Cash Flow

Disney DIS and Amazon AMZN face similar trade-offs. Disney projects fiscal 2026 content spend of about $24 billion, alongside roughly $9 billion of capital expenditures. Disney's fiscal third-quarter free cash flow rose 63% to $3.1 billion, though nine-month free cash flow declined 24% to $5.7 billion amid higher tax payments and sports content spending. Amazon is backing Prime Video with live sports, including Thursday Night Football and NBA on Prime, but its cash profile is driven largely by infrastructure investment. Amazon reported a trailing 12-month free cash outflow of $42.4 billion and still expects 2026 cash capital expenditures of approximately $220 billion.

Story Continues

news.Title: Strategy Expands Cloud Subscriptions: Can Software Revenues Recover?
news.Content:
Strategy Inc. MSTR is witnessing strong growth in its cloud subscription business as customers increasingly migrate from traditional on-premises software licenses to cloud-based services. However, declining product license and support revenues continue to weigh on overall software performance, raising questions about the pace of recovery.

In the third quarter of 2026, subscription services revenues surged 49.2% year over year to $68.6 million, accounting for nearly 55% of total software revenues. However, overall software revenues declined 2.6% to $125.4 million. Product license revenues plunged 77.9% to $3.8 million, while product support revenues fell 26.3% to $37.7 million. The growth in subscriptions has not yet fully offset weakness in legacy offerings.

The cloud transition is gaining traction. Subscription revenues increased 53.6% to $190.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, lifting their contribution to total software revenues to 51.2% from 35% a year earlier. Higher cloud adoption, increased usage by existing customers and new contracts are supporting this growth. Subscription gross margin also improved to 72% from 57.4% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting better profitability in the expanding business.

Strategy's cloud-native analytics platform, Strategy Mosaic and generative AI capabilities offer additional opportunities to strengthen customer engagement and drive subscription adoption. However, the company faces challenges from customer attrition, rising cloud infrastructure expenses and competition.

Strategy's software business is making progress toward a recurring-revenue model, but a sustained recovery remains uncertain. Continued subscription growth, improved underlying profitability and the ability to offset declining legacy revenues will be critical to restoring momentum.

How Are Strategy's Competitors Faring?

Microsoft MSFT reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $92.3 billion, up 19% year over year. Microsoft Cloud revenues increased 30% to $63.9 billion, while Azure revenues surged 48%. Its Power BI and Microsoft Fabric platforms offer cloud analytics, data integration and AI-powered capabilities, intensifying competition with Strategy's enterprise software business.

Salesforce CRM reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $11.3 billion, up 11% year over year. Subscription and support revenues rose 12% to $10.8 billion. Agentforce and Data 360 annual recurring revenues came in at $3.9 billion. Its Tableau platforms provide cloud-based analytics and AI-driven insights, challenging Strategy's software offerings.

Story Continues

Strategy shares have gained 26% over the past three months, outperforming the broader industry and the S&P 500 Index.

In terms of forward 12-month Price/Earnings (P/E), MSTR is currently trading at 5.1X, which is at a discount to the industry average of 13X.

Strategy's estimate revisions reflect a positive trend. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 EPS has been revised upward significantly over the past month. The consensus estimate calls for 14.6% growth year over year.
