news.Title: What Bitdeer Technologies Group (BTDR) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Bitdeer Technologies Group? Here are five stocks we like better.

Revenue reached a record $320.7 million , up 89% year over year, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $69.6 million. Bitdeer still reported a $125.5 million net loss amid heavy investment.

Management cited about $7.6 billion in expected contracted AI revenue and 332 IT megawatts of secured data-center capacity. AI cloud revenue grew 46% sequentially to $20.4 million, while construction and customer installations at key sites are scheduled to ramp from late 2026 into 2027.

Spending sharply reduced cash to $163.7 million from $456.8 million as quarterly capital expenditures reached $478 million and debt rose to $1.95 billion. Bitdeer is pursuing project and asset-level financing, while lowering its 2026 crypto-mining infrastructure capex outlook to $200 million or less.

4 Blockchain Stocks That Aren't Coinbase

Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR) reported record third-quarter revenue as Bitcoin production and co-mining expanded, while management outlined plans to finance a growing pipeline of artificial intelligence infrastructure projects.

Revenue rose 89% year over year to $320.7 million, and adjusted EBITDA increased to $69.6 million from $25.5 million a year earlier. The company posted a net loss of $125.5 million, or $0.46 per share, as it invested heavily in data centers and computing equipment.

→ The Ugly Truth Behind SoundHound's Q3 Results

Beyond the Halving: The Future of Bitcoin Mining Stocks

Chief Strategy Officer Haris Basit said Bitdeer's AI platform represents approximately $7.6 billion in expected contracted revenue: about $4.7 billion from the base term of its Tydal data center lease in Norway and $2.9 billion in AI cloud backlog. The two businesses have different revenue recognition profiles and capital requirements, he said.

AI Cloud Contracts and Tydal Construction

AI cloud revenue increased 46% from the second quarter to $20.4 million. Bitdeer ended September with 4,328 graphics processing units deployed at approximately 95% utilization. The business generated $3.1 million in gross profit, compared with a $2.3 million gross loss in the prior quarter.

→ Lemonade's Revenue Soars 73%—So Why Did Its Stock Turn Sour After Earnings?

Chief Financial Officer Michael Potter said the sequential revenue increase came primarily from pricing and customer mix as utilization of higher-value systems rose. AI cloud annualized recurring revenue was approximately $86 million at quarter-end.

Story Continues

In Malaysia, Bitdeer has sold out the 9.5 megawatts of capacity at its A102 facility under five-year commitments representing more than $800 million in expected revenue. More than 70% of the 21.7 megawatts at A201 is contracted, representing over $1.7 billion in expected five-year revenue. The company expects revenue to begin at A102 in the first quarter of 2027 and at A201 in the second quarter.

→ Anthropic's S-1 Strengthens the Case for Broadcom's AI Growth

Potter said secured AI cloud data center capacity has reached approximately 332 IT megawatts, or about 95% of the company's target for the first quarter of 2028. He cautioned that secured capacity, which includes owned sites and those covered by executed data center services agreements, is not the same as capacity contracted to customers.

At Tydal, phase-one delivery remains scheduled for year-end, with customer installations planned to begin in January. Phase-two data hall deliveries are expected to start at the end of the first quarter of 2027. The lease with Volta covers 121 IT megawatts over 16 years, subject to the tenant's right to terminate without a fee after 10 years.

Potter said Bitdeer has begun the project-financing process. He also said Volta's reported GPU financing removed a major item needed to activate the anticipated letter-of-credit support, with construction completion and operational GPUs among the remaining steps.

Cash Declines as Spending Rises

Bitdeer ended the quarter with $163.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $456.8 million at the end of the second quarter. Capital expenditures totaled $478 million, including approximately $288 million for data center construction and land and about $110 million for SEALMINER production. Total debt rose to $1.95 billion.

Potter said cash declined because the company funded Tydal construction and a land purchase at Rockdale ahead of expected financing. Operating cash flow was approximately $6 million, including customer prepayments. The company also sold $221.5 million of mined Bitcoin, proceeds reported in investing activities.

Management expects customer prepayments and asset-level financing to support AI cloud deployments. Potter said financing for the A102 GPUs was in its final stages, while work was underway on a similar arrangement for A201. Deferred revenue, mostly AI cloud prepayments, reached approximately $342 million at quarter-end.

During the call, Potter gave differing figures for remaining Tydal construction spending, citing approximately $350 million and approximately $250 million in prepared remarks, then about $500 million during questions. He did not reconcile the figures. He said the company would seek at least $500 million in financing and hoped to recover some equity previously invested in the site, subject to market conditions.

Bitdeer raised $58 million through its at-the-market equity program in the third quarter, compared with $457 million in the second. Potter said the company had not recently accessed equity markets but declined to rule out future equity financing.

Mining Growth and Capital Outlook

Bitdeer mined 3,855 Bitcoin during the quarter, up 43% from the second quarter, while co-mining revenue rose 140% sequentially to $59.9 million. Self-mining hash rate reached approximately 82.3 exahash per second at quarter-end.

Power cost per Bitcoin mined was approximately $36,000, down from $49,000 a year earlier, as fleet efficiency improved. Total gross profit was $10.8 million, reversing a second-quarter gross loss, although average power costs rose to 4.7 cents per kilowatt-hour from 4.4 cents.

The company now expects 2026 crypto mining infrastructure capital spending at or below $200 million, the low end of its previous $200 million to $280 million range. The forecast excludes SEALMINER hardware, GPUs, AI cloud and high-performance computing infrastructure. Potter said Bitdeer plans to provide 2027 guidance with its fourth-quarter results.

Founder and CEO Jihan Wu said Bitdeer expects to slow the pace of new crypto-mining capital investment next year while continuing to expand operations. At Rockdale, he said the company plans to seek additional grid power and build new AI data centers on acquired land rather than broadly winding down existing mining operations.

About Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR)

Bitdeer Technologies Group is a technology company focused on cryptocurrency mining and related infrastructure. Its business includes operating mining data centers, mining digital assets for its own account, and providing hosting services that allow customers to deploy and operate mining equipment.

The company also develops and sells cryptocurrency mining machines and offers cloud hash rate services, which provide customers access to computing capacity for mining without requiring them to operate the equipment themselves.

news.Title: CEO Lip-Bu Tan’s 150,000-Share Purchase Wasn’t Enough to Stop the Slide in Intel Stock
news.Content:
Intel (INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan might have theorized that the sharp downturn in Intel stock had made its shares a value pick, and that his recent move to buy 150,000 shares of INTC stock could rescue it from a further downfall. However, shares fell even further after his Nov. 2 purchase, dropping as much as 10% on Nov. 5 alone before staging a recovery in the following days.

Intel stock now trades at around $59 per share, down roughly 8% from the average price of $64.73 at which Tan purchased his new shares. Notably, the CEO parted with about $9.71 million for the transaction. While a wider market selloff targeting the artificial intelligence (AI) trade could be seen as a reason for the recent downturn, that is not the whole picture. Let's take a closer look.

More News from Barchart

Nvidia Stock Could Shed Up to $225 Billion Over Jensen Huang Probe, But Rival AMD's Rally Shows It's Not an AI Demand Problem

Dear D-Wave Quantum Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Dan Ives Sees Just a 15% Chance Nvidia Loses Jensen Huang — But His Removal Could Erase 30% of The Stock's Value

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

About Intel Stock

Founded in 1968, Intel is an integrated semiconductor company that designs, manufactures, packages, and sells processors and other semiconductor products. Its business can broadly be understood through two major segments; Intel Products designs and sells processors and related semiconductor products to customers, while Intel Foundry manufactures and packages semiconductors — from chips designed by Intel itself to those designed by external customers.

Valued at a market capitalization of $299 billion, INTC stock is up 61% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. Having said that, the stock's upward momentum so far this year may now be dragging its heels.

How Intel Is Falling Short

Intel's 18A process of making chips was supposed to bring its foundry business to life with external customers. Intel claimed that the 18A methodology delivers up to 18% higher performance at the same power, 38% lower power at the same performance, and 30% greater chip density compared with Intel 3. However, that has not resulted in Intel meaningfully competing with market leader Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM).

At the end of 2025, Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) disclosed that it had "deployed 305 distinct process technologies, and manufactured 12,682 products for 534 customers," with 74% of wafer revenue coming from 7 nanometer-and-below technologies. Although Intel does not disclose comparable figures, the latest quarterly results for both firms bear testament to TSMC's scale.

Story Continues

For the third quarter of 2026, TSMC saw revenue of $46.72 billion, compared to Intel's foundry revenue from external customers of just $411 million during the same period. That's a stark difference. Moreover, TSMC's CoWoS packaging technology has become the industry standard, competing with Intel's own advanced packaging technologies, such as EMIB and Foveros.

Of course, TSMC is a pure-play foundry player, whereas Intel has interests in other aspects of the chip supply chain. Yet, in that regard, Intel is also lagging behind the leading duo of Nvidia (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD).

In GPUs, Nvidia's moat has been its CUDA ecosystem, which has been around for two decades now. On the other hand, Intel's oneAPI and related software initiatives have not achieved comparable developer adoption in AI accelerator workloads. Intel's hardware has also not established the same combination of performance, memory capacity, bandwidth, and system-level scalability that Nvidia offers. AI customers are increasingly buying complete computing systems rather than individual chips, and Nvidia has been particularly successful in offering integrated GPU, networking, and software platforms. Thus, customers who have already invested heavily in Nvidia's ecosystem are not willing to shift to Intel's so easily.

In the realm of CPUs, AMD has also emerged as a serious contender. Intel's historical advantage was its ability to introduce new processor architectures alongside leading-edge manufacturing improvements. But delays in its manufacturing roadmap have meant inconsistent delivery of improvements in transistor density, performance, and power efficiency. Meanwhile, AMD has adopted a fabless model and outsourced manufacturing to TSMC. This has allowed it to use TSMC's advanced manufacturing processes without having to fund its own leading-edge fab facilities.

Specifically, AMD's chiplet approach has been a major competitive advantage because it allows the company to manufacture multiple smaller compute dies rather than relying entirely on a large monolithic die. Although Intel has also adopted chiplets, the distinction is that AMD has demonstrated a successful commercial model around the technology for several generations.

Intel's Q3 Double Beat Was Not Enough

Intel's latest Q3 2026 results were good on the surface, with both revenue and earnings beating estimates. Yet investors were disappointed with Q4 guidance, causing INTC stock to plummet almost 29% in the next trading session.

Revenue for the quarter was $16.5 billion, up 21% from the prior-year period. Data-center revenue continued to show strong momentum, rising 78% on a year-over-year (YOY) basis to $7.3 billion. Total foundry revenue came in at $6.7 billion, up a healthy 58%. Still, only $411 million came from external customers, signaling that Intel still has a long way to go to become a key player in chip manufacturing again.

Earnings jumped to $0.52 per share from $0.23 per share in the prior year, outpacing the consensus estimate of $0.40 per share. However, Q4 guidance of $15 billion to $16 billion in revenue and earnings of $0.25 per share disappointed.

Net cash from operating activities for the nine months ended Sept. 26, 2026 came in at $24.8 billion, a jump from $5.1 billion a year ago. Free cash flow for the three months ended Sept. 26, 2026 was also $1.6 billion, up from $896 million in the prior year. Yet Intel's gross capital expenditures in the period were $4.2 billion, while the company continues to forecast capex of $20 billion for 2026. Accordingly, Intel's cash requirements continue to be substantial. Overall, Intel closed the quarter with a cash balance of $21.8 billion, much higher than its short-term debt of $3.8 billion.

Meanwhile, INTC stock trades at overvalued levels. Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 50.3 times, price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 5.2 times, and price-to-cash flow (P/CF) ratio of 23.3 times all trade above the respective sector medians.

What Do Analysts Think of Intel Stock?

Overall, analysts have a consensus "Hold" rating for INTC stock. Out of 46 analysts covering the stock, nine have a "Strong Buy" rating, one has a "Moderate Buy" rating, 35 have a "Hold" rating, and one analyst has a "Strong Sell" rating. The mean target price of $93.23 denotes potential upside of 57% from current levels.

news.Title: INTC vs. TSM: Which Semiconductor Stock Has More Upside Now?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM are two premier semiconductor manufacturers competing in advanced chip fabrication and foundry services. Both are competing hard in the AI-powered chipmaking market, with Intel expanding its foundry business and TSM dominating the contract chipmaking market.

Intel is currently focusing on AI chips for data centers and PCs, which marks one of the largest architectural shifts for the company in 40 years. The decision is primarily aimed at gaining a firmer footing in the expansive AI sector, spanning cloud and enterprise servers to networks, volume clients and ubiquitous edge environments, in tune with the evolving market dynamics. The foundry operating model is a key component of the company's strategy and is designed to reshape operational dynamics and drive greater transparency, accountability and focus on costs and efficiency.

TSM is benefiting from accelerating AI investments, growing demand for advanced semiconductor technologies and aggressive global manufacturing expansion. The company's technological leadership, strong profitability and robust demand outlook position it favorably for sustained growth.

Let us try to analyze some of the competitive strengths and weaknesses of the companies to understand who is in a better position to maximize gains from the emerging market trends.

The Case for INTC

Intel is witnessing healthy traction in AI PCs that have taken the market by storm. Its innovative AI solutions are set to benefit the broader semiconductor ecosystem by driving down costs, improving performance and fostering an open, scalable AI environment. The proliferation of generative AI applications is driving significant investments in data center infrastructure. Although GPUs remain at the center of AI computing, CPUs continue to play an important role in supporting AI workloads. This is creating incremental opportunities for Intel's Xeon portfolio. The momentum is encouraging as AI-related infrastructure spending is likely to remain healthy, providing Intel with an opportunity to capitalize on rising compute requirements.

Intel is ramping Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake products based on its advanced 18A process technology. Increasing adoption of these products, coupled with an eventual enterprise PC refresh cycle, should support the client business over the long run. The company is also expanding its presence in edge computing and physical AI applications, including robotics. These emerging markets could broaden Intel's addressable opportunity beyond traditional PCs.

However, Intel derives a significant part of its revenues from China. As Washington tightens restrictions on high-tech exports to China, Beijing has intensified its push for self-sufficiency in critical industries. This shift poses a dual challenge for Intel, as it faces potential market restrictions and increased competition from domestic chipmakers. The company is also lagging in the GPU and AI front compared to peers, such as NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD. Leading technology companies are reportedly piling up NVIDIA's GPUs to build computing clusters for their AI work, driving exponential revenue growth.

Story Continues

The Case for TSM

TSM remains a key beneficiary of accelerating investments in AI infrastructure. Growing demand for AI accelerators, custom chips, networking processors and agentic AI applications is driving the adoption of its advanced manufacturing technologies. TSM's leadership in cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing provides a significant competitive advantage. Management expects N2-family annual capacity to more than double in 2027, supported by robust smartphone and HPC/AI demand. Its next-generation A14 technology remains on track for risk production in 2027 and volume production in 2028, strengthening long-term growth opportunities.

TSM is accelerating manufacturing investments to capitalize on sustained semiconductor demand. The company reiterated its 2026 capital expenditure budget of $60-$64 billion and expects investments during 2026-2028 to significantly exceed those of the preceding three years. The company is developing nearly 20 fabrication facilities globally. Its second Arizona fab is scheduled to begin volume production in the third quarter of 2027, while an additional 3-nanometer capacity in Taiwan is expected to become operational during 2027 and 2028. These investments should strengthen supply capabilities and support future revenue growth.

However, TSM faces headwinds from rising manufacturing costs, significant capital expenditure requirements and ongoing global capacity expansion. The expansion of overseas manufacturing facilities, particularly in the United States, is expected to increase gross margin dilution to 3-4 percentage points over the next few years, compared with approximately 2 percentage points anticipated for 2026. Elevated spending could constrain free cash flow generation and weigh on returns if demand growth fails to keep pace with capacity additions. Moreover, rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainties are pressuring consumer-oriented and price-sensitive end markets, prompting management to adopt a cautious approach toward 2027 business planning. These factors could limit near-term margin expansion and profitability despite robust demand for advanced semiconductor technologies.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for INTC & TSM?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Intel's 2026 sales implies year-over-year growth of 17%, while that for EPS indicates a surge of 250%. The EPS estimates have trended down 2% over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for TSM's 2026 sales indicates year-over-year growth of 42%, while that for EPS suggests a rise of 63.9%. The EPS estimates have trended up 5.5% over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of INTC & TSM

Over the past year, Intel has surged 56.8% against the industry's decline of 0.2%. TSM has gained 33.5% over the same period.

One-Year INTC, TSM Stock Price Performance

Intel looks more attractive than TSM from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, Intel's shares currently trade at 4.65 forward sales, lower than 9.01 for TSM.

INTC or TSM: Which is a Better Pick?

Intel currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), while TSM carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Both Intel and TSM expect revenues and earnings to improve in 2026. In terms of price performance, Intel has outperformed TSM and is trading relatively cheaply. However, with a better Zacks rank, solid fundamentals and healthy growth potential, TSM appears to be relatively better placed than Intel. Consequently, TSM is a better investment option at the moment.

news.Title: Don’t Chase the Arm Stock Dip Yet. What Patient Investors Should Wait for Before They Buy.
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (ARM) just did everything right on paper, and the stock still tanked. The stock fell more than 11% on Thursday right after the earnings report.

In its fiscal second-quarter report, Arm delivered revenue of $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year and above the $1.38 billion analysts were expecting. Adjusted earnings per share hit $0.52, up from $0.39 a year ago and ahead of the $0.47 consensus.

More News from Barchart

Nvidia Stock Could Shed Up to $225 Billion Over Jensen Huang Probe, But Rival AMD's Rally Shows It's Not an AI Demand Problem

Dear D-Wave Quantum Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Dan Ives Sees Just a 15% Chance Nvidia Loses Jensen Huang — But His Removal Could Erase 30% of The Stock's Value

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

So, yes, Arm topped estimates on both revenue and EPS. Still, investors headed for the exit. That's a puzzling reaction, but a closer look at the numbers explains it.

Why Arm Stock is Sinking

The selling momentum was not abated after just one poor session; ARM stock is down by over 42% in the last month, but is still up by nearly 60% for the year.

The stock reached a 52-week high of over $450 earlier this year, fueled by the soaring frenzy surrounding artificial intelligence, but has returned most of it. That indicates that the rally was a weak one.

Add to that a frosty atmosphere behind them. The demand for phones is being impacted by high pricing of memory, which has been under pressure in the broad chip industry. In addition, the royalties failed to take off. The increase in royalty revenue was 8% to $670 million, which was less than the estimated 13% increase Arm told investors in July.

Turning to valuation, Arm isn't cheap, even after the drop. Its Price-to-Earnings (P/E) is 83x, far higher than the sector median of 21x, while its Price-to-Sales is 33x, compared to the sector median of 3.1x. These stretched ratios indicate ARM shares trade at a significant premium, making the stock very costly for new investors.

What's Really Happening Under the Hood

The most important thing is that it was an authentic beat, but it wasn't from the right spot. The numbers for licenses, which pay for the rights to use equipment, increased 50% to $773 million, compared with only an 8% increase for royalties, the category that correlates with the number of chips sold.

Licensing is lumpy. Investors pay the stream of revenues called royalties. Last fiscal year, smartphones accounted for approximately 43% of the royalty revenue, while the actual revenue from royalties was relatively unchanged.

Story Continues

Guidance didn't help either. Third-quarter Arm revenue is expected at $1.54 billion, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) are forecast at $0.56, still just a hair below the midpoint of the $1.53 billion and $0.55 reported consensus.

Arm's Bigger Plan Beyond Phones

The good news is that Arm is no longer just a licensor. Its first real chip, the Arm AGI CPU, is built for agentic AI, with Meta Platforms (META) as the lead customer and shipments starting in the fiscal fourth quarter.

Arm now expects up to $2 billion in cumulative AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028, double its prior forecast. The long-term target is $15 billion a year by fiscal 2031.

Elsewhere, data center royalties doubled and now make up about a quarter of the total, while physical AI royalties grew 50% on auto strength. However, first-generation gross margins should be just 30% to 40%, and real volume doesn't arrive until fiscal 2028.

Wall Street Can't Agree on Arm Stock

There is a divide among analysts, and it is growing. Among the most vocal bears is Goldman Sachs, which still has a $160 target and a Sell rating. It argues that the price is slow to move and more often than not, that price is determined by licensing, not royalties or by using an AGI CPU.

More conservative groups have been Morgan Stanley, which maintained an Overweight rating on the stock but reduced its target price to $245 from $255. It noted that results were solid, with a 50% increase in licensing revenue to $773 million, as well as several AGI CPU purchase orders and a new SoftBank project.

Lee Simpson of Morgan Stanley held an Equal-Weight rating and a $212 target, noting execution concerns with scaling up production of CPUs. Susquehanna's Mehdi Hosseini maintained a Positive rating on Arm and kept the $320 target unchanged, topping their list with Arm's aim to ramp up to $2 billion of AGI CPU sales by fiscal 2028.

The 32 analysts have a consensus "Moderate Buy," and the 12-month average price target is $270, which suggests the stock could climb up to 74% from here. We have targets from $130 to $480, so no one agrees on what Arm is worth.

news.Title: ONTO Beats Q3 Estimates & Uplifts View: Buy, Hold or Sell the Stock?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation Inc. ONTO delivered stronger-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, with revenues, operating margin and earnings per share exceeding the high end of management's guidance. Strong demand for AI-related semiconductor manufacturing equipment, growing adoption of its Dragonfly inspection platform and rising investments in advanced packaging supported the performance. Revenues reached $410 million, up nearly 90% year over year and 19% sequentially.

Non-GAAP earnings per share increased to $2.44 from 92 cents in the prior-year quarter, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.6% from 21.1%. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 57.6%, increasing 60 bps sequentially and 360 bps year over year. Continued margin expansion could support further earnings growth if demand remains strong and ONTO maintains operating efficiency. The company's outlook also strengthened, with management raising its fourth-quarter revenue expectations and reporting a record backlog of more than $1.3 billion. Improving customer visibility, expanding product adoption and operational efficiencies are expected to support growth through 2027.

In response to a record third quarter, ONTO's shares jumped 12% in last day's trading and closed at $194.04. Shares also went up 6% in pre-market trading today. ONTO's shares have risen 45.4% in the past year compared with the Zacks Nanotechnology industry's growth of 46.5%. The company has outpaced the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the S&P 500 composite's growth of 6.4% and 0.9%, respectively.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ONTO's key competitors include KLA Corporation KLAC, Camtek Ltd CAMT and Applied Materials AMAT. KLAC, CAMT, and AMAT grew 27.1%, 0.9%, and 62%, respectively, over the same period.

However, after this strong performance, investors may question whether ONTO shares still have room to rise. Let's examine the company's growth drivers, financial performance and potential risks to assess its investment prospects.

Strong Q3 Results Highlight ONTO's Growth Momentum

The results reflect strong demand across the company's product portfolio. Advanced packaging and specialty device products were the key contributors, with revenues increasing 35% sequentially. These businesses accounted for slightly more than half of total quarterly revenues, led by continued Dragonfly adoption and a recovery in power and specialty device inspection demand. Advanced-node revenues reached approximately $135 million, with memory contributing about 60% and logic accounting for the remaining 40%. Software and services generated roughly $60 million.

Story Continues

An encouraging indicator is Onto Innovation's backlog, which increased to more than $1.3 billion during the third quarter. Management cited strong customer demand and visibility into investment plans extending multiple years. It expects full-year 2026 revenue growth to exceed 45% year over year and anticipates sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027. These expectations are backed by demand for advanced packaging, increasingly sophisticated logic and memory devices, and inspection technologies that help manufacturers improve process control. Management also expects advanced packaging revenues to grow more than 80% in 2026, while Advanced Nodes revenues are expected to increase more than 35%. These projections highlight the breadth of the company's growth opportunities.

The Dragonfly platform, especially G5, led growth, supporting high-resolution applications with more than 10 customers and orders extending into 2027. The G5 platform is increasingly adopted for new applications, with revenues doubling compared with 2025, while G3 remains relevant for lower-end needs. ONTO also reported strong momentum in power semiconductors and silicon photonics. Combined revenues from these markets doubled in the third quarter, with management expecting significant growth in the fourth quarter and into the first half of 2027.

Onto Innovation Inc. Price and Consensus

Onto Innovation Inc. price-consensus-chart | Onto Innovation Inc. Quote

The strong order visibility prompted ONTO to raise its fourth-quarter 2026 revenue outlook. It expects fourth-quarter revenues of $430-$450 million, representing more than 7% sequential growth at the midpoint. At the midpoint of its guidance, gross margin is expected to improve around 50 bps sequentially to slightly above 58%, while operating margin is projected to reach 34%. ONTO also forecasts non-GAAP EPS of $2.69.

For full-year 2026, management expects revenues of about $1.485 billion at the midpoint, representing growth of more than 45%. Looking ahead, ONTO anticipates sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027, supported by strong customer commitments, broader product adoption and a growing backlog.

What Could Limit ONTO's Growth Upside?

Despite its strong growth outlook, it faces several risks that investors should consider. Onto Innovation faces several cost and operational headwinds, including rising memory and component prices, higher freight expenses, tariffs and dependence on certain single-source components. Although the company is addressing these challenges through product design changes, localized supply chains, supplier partnerships and operational efficiencies, persistent cost pressures or component shortages could affect margins and equipment deliveries.

Demand uncertainty is another risk, as any slowdown or delay in data center and AI infrastructure investments could weaken customer spending and order momentum. In addition, technology transitions, including upgrades to newer inspection systems and evolving advanced packaging methods, require continuous innovation and operational adjustments. While productivity improvements, extended factory models and supply-chain initiatives have helped mitigate these pressures, their impact on profitability and growth remains worth monitoring.

Additionally, the company must manage execution and delivery risks to convert its record backlog into revenues on schedule. Rapid technological changes and competition in inspection and metrology also require continued innovation to maintain its position in advanced packaging and advanced-node markets.

Valuation risk

Strong growth expectations may already be reflected in the stock price. Even solid earnings results may not produce additional upside if expectations are too high. In terms of forward price/earnings, ONTO's shares are trading at 17.32X, higher than the industry's 3.37X.

KLAC, CAMT and AMAT are trading at multiples of 24.44X, 23.72X and 20.12X, respectively.

Estimate Revision Trend for ONTO

Earnings estimates for ONTO have been stagnant for both 2026 and 2027 over the past 60 days.

ONTO Stock After Q3 Results: Buy, Hold or Sell?

ONTO's record backlog, AI-driven demand and higher 2027 growth visibility support a bullish business outlook, but the stock's valuation and execution risks matter before making a Buy call. Investors should monitor the sustainability of AI-related semiconductor spending, customer investment plans, execution as the company scales and its ability to maintain margin expansion. The company's strong operating outlook is encouraging, but the potential for further stock gains also depends on its valuation and market expectations.

Existing shareholders may consider holding the stock as long as the company's growth outlook remains strong and its valuation is reasonable. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), ONTO appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and new investors may be better off trading with caution. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: ASTS Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Higher Costs Offset Revenue Growth
news.Content:
AST SpaceMobile, Inc. ASTS reported lackluster third-quarter 2026 results, with both earnings and revenues missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. The company reported a loss of 44 cents per share, wider than the consensus estimate of a loss of 41 cents, representing a negative surprise of 7.3%. However, the loss narrowed from 45 cents per share in the year-ago quarter.

Quarterly revenues surged 187.1% year over year to $42.32 million but missed the consensus estimate of $44.47 million by 4.8%. Growth was driven by commercial gateway deliveries and U.S. government contract milestones. However, elevated operating expenses continued to pressure profitability.

ASTS Sees Robust Growth Across Revenue Streams

Product revenues increased 165.6% year over year to $20.57 million from $7.75 million in the prior-year quarter. Growth was primarily driven by commercial gateway equipment deliveries to mobile network operator partners as the company expanded its ground infrastructure.

Service revenues surged 211% to $21.75 million from $6.99 million a year ago. The increase reflected progress in U.S. government programs and the achievement of contractual milestones. The company continues to benefit from growing demand for its space-based communication and sensing capabilities.

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Quote

AST SpaceMobile's Operating Costs Remain Elevated

Total operating expenses increased 123.5% year over year to $211.03 million from $94.42 million. Engineering services costs surged 134.6% to $95.79 million, reflecting investments in satellite manufacturing, workforce expansion and network development.

General and administrative expenses increased 86.8% to $55.71 million. Research and development expenses rose to $9.09 million from $5.53 million. Depreciation and amortization expenses increased to $25.08 million from $12.72 million.

Adjusted operating expenses were $133.6 million, up from $119.1 million in the preceding quarter. Excluding adjusted cost of revenues, adjusted operating expenses totaled $109.4 million, within management's previously guided range of $105 million to $115 million.

ASTS Advances Satellite Manufacturing and Deployment

AST SpaceMobile accelerated its satellite manufacturing roadmap by advancing next-generation application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) integration to BlueBird 34 from the originally planned BlueBird 50. The upgraded technology is expected to deliver a 10-fold improvement in processing bandwidth compared with its existing Block 1 satellites.

The company is manufacturing satellites through BlueBird 51 at its Texas facilities. Two factories are operating full shifts, supporting management's target of producing six ASIC-enabled satellites monthly by December 2026.

Story Continues

BlueBirds 14, 15 and 16 have been shipped to Cape Canaveral, while additional satellite shipments are planned through January 2027. Management targets approximately 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by mid-2027, with launch agreements covering more than 100 satellites for deployment during 2027 and 2028.

AST SpaceMobile Expands Commercial and Government Reach

The company expects to activate intermittent nationwide satellite broadband coverage in the United States and other key markets before the end of 2026. Initial rollout markets include Canada, Japan, Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom.

AST SpaceMobile has agreements with more than 60 mobile network operators representing over three billion subscribers globally. It also successfully validated satellite beam handovers between terrestrial and space-based cellular networks with AT&T, marking an important step toward commercial service deployment.

Government opportunities are expanding. The company secured an approximately $100 million U.S. Space Force contract for advanced space-based sensing capabilities. It also announced approximately $1 billion in non-dilutive Japanese government funding to support mid-band satellite manufacturing and launches.

ASTS Maintains Strong Liquidity Amid Heavy Investments

As of Sept. 30, 2026, AST SpaceMobile held approximately $3.23 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. Long-term debt, excluding the current portion, stood at $4.08 billion compared with $2.21 billion at the end of 2025.

Capital expenditures totaled approximately $310 million during the third quarter, down from approximately $610 million in the preceding quarter. The lower spending primarily reflected timing-related shifts in launch payments.

The company also announced Blacklift, its planned reusable rocket capable of carrying up to five BlueBird satellites per launch. Initial launches are targeted for late 2028, potentially providing greater control over satellite deployment schedules.

AST SpaceMobile Reaffirms 2026 Revenue Outlook

Management reiterated its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150 million to $200 million, with potential upside from recently signed contracts. Revenue generation is expected to benefit from gateway deliveries, government contract milestones, consulting services and software licensing.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, AST SpaceMobile expects adjusted operating expenses, excluding adjusted cost of revenues, between $130 million and $140 million. Capital expenditures are projected between $400 million and $500 million, reflecting continued satellite production and launch-related investments.

Zacks Rank

AST SpaceMobile currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Cisco has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 10.88%. The company delivered an average earnings surprise of 2.55% in the last four reported quarters.

NVIDIA Corporation NVDA is set to release third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 17. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at $2.49 per share, implying growth of 100.8% from the year-ago reported figure.

NVIDIA has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 14%. The company delivered an average earnings surprise of 5.82% in the last four reported quarters.

Keysight Technologies, Inc. KEYS is scheduled to release fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings on Nov. 19. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at $3.36 per share, suggesting growth of 75.92% from the year-ago reported figure.

The discounted valuation remains despite HPE stock climbing 98% year to date, outperforming the broader sector and the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry's return of 65.2% and 4.1%, respectively.

HPE YTD Performance Chart

HPE Experiences Growth Across Cloud and Networking

Hewlett Packard Enterprise operates across three primary business segments, namely Cloud & AI, Networking, and Corporate Investments and Other, serving enterprise customers with infrastructure, software, services and flexible consumption solutions. Cloud & AI combines HPE's server, storage and financial services businesses.

HPE's server portfolio includes general-purpose and workload-optimized systems, high-performance computing, supercomputing, AI infrastructure, data analytics and transaction processing. Its storage offerings include HPE Alletra, unstructured data solutions, data protection, GreenLake Flex and related software. The segment is benefiting from growing demand for AI-ready servers and enterprise infrastructure. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Cloud & AI generated $9.04 billion in revenues, up 25.4% year over year.

HPE's networking develops and sells network and security products and services across campus, branch, data center, routing and security markets. Its portfolio includes wireless access points, switches, routers, gateways, network-management software, support and professional services. The acquisition of Juniper Networks has expanded HPE's networking capabilities and exposure to AI data center infrastructure. HPE's networking revenues reached $2.89 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, rising 10% on a normalized basis.

Corporate Investments and Other includes Advisory and Professional Services, Telco, Instant On and Hewlett Packard Labs. These activities complement HPE's broader technology portfolio through consulting, specialized connectivity offerings and research. Across these businesses, HPE is also expanding GreenLake, its consumption-based hybrid cloud platform, connecting infrastructure, software and services. Together, its three segments position HPE to address demand for AI infrastructure, modern networking and hybrid cloud environments.

Story Continues

HPE Wins Against Competitors With Diverse Portfolio

HPE competes with Super Micro Computer SMCI, Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO in the AI infrastructure market. However, HPE's ability to package compute, storage, networking and services into pre-configured solutions can reduce deployment complexity for enterprises and sovereign customers while giving it an edge over its competitors. Super Micro Computer is on track to scale rack production capacity to more than 6,000 AI racks per month by the end of fiscal 2026, including 3,000 direct liquid cooling racks monthly.

Super Micro Computer is already shipping 150kW AI racks in volume and preparing 250kW and 500kW rack solutions to support future high-density AI training and inference workloads. Dell Technologies is a major supplier of servers and storage systems, with a broad customer base across enterprises and cloud providers. Its scale, established distribution and service offerings give it an edge in winning large contracts.

Cisco has also taken $5.3 billion of hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in fiscal 2026 and raised its full-year order outlook to $9 billion from $5 billion. However, HPE's ability to package compute, storage, networking and services into pre-configured solutions can reduce deployment complexity for enterprises and sovereign customers. This gives HPE an edge over its competitors.

HPE is also able to keep its margin stable. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for HPE's fiscal 2026 margin reflects year-over-year growth of 97%. Estimates have been revised upward over the past 30 days.

Conclusion: Buy HPE Stock Now

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's strong AI infrastructure momentum, expanding AI backlog, growing GreenLake adoption and integrated portfolio support its growth outlook. Despite a sharp share price rally, HPE's valuation remains attractive relative to industry peers. Given these factors, it's prudent to accumulate this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock at present. news.Title: Here's How Much a $1000 Investment in Monolithic Power Made 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
news.Content:
How much a stock's price changes over time is a significant driver for most investors. Not only can price performance impact your portfolio, but it can help you compare investment results across sectors and industries as well.

Another thing that can drive investing is the fear of missing out, or FOMO. This particularly applies to tech giants and popular consumer-facing stocks.

What if you'd invested in Monolithic Power (MPWR) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to MPWR for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?

Monolithic Power's Business In-Depth

With that in mind, let's take a look at Monolithic Power's main business drivers.

Monolithic Power Systems designs, develops and markets high-performance power solutions. The company focuses on the market for high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits (ICs).

Monolithic's products are widely used in industrial applications, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud computing, and automotive and consumer applications.

Being a fabless company, Monolithic works with third-party contractors and chip assemblers for the manufacturing, assembling and testing of wafers and ICs. This approach permits the company to focus more on the designing and development of process technology at a lower fixed cost.

Unlike other fabless semiconductor companies, Monolithic installs its own proprietary process technologies in third-party contractors' equipment and facilities.

Monolithic reported total revenues of $1,202.4 million in the third quarter of 2026.

Its key product families include DC-to-DC, AC-to-DC, driver metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor, power management IC, current-limit switch and lighting-control products.

DC-to-DC ICs are used to convert and control voltages within a broad range of electronic systems, such as portable electronic devices, wireless LAN access points, computers and monitors, automobiles and medical equipment.

Lighting control ICs are used in backlighting and general illumination products.

By end market, 42.1% of total revenues came from Enterprise Data in the third quarter of 2026.

Storage and Computing, Consumer, Industrial, Automotive and Communications end-markets contributed 16.0%, 5.3%, 6.0%, 15.0% and 15.6%, respectively, to the third quarter of 2026 revenues.

Monolithic's primary competitors are Analog Devices, Infineon Technologies, NXP Semiconductors, ON Semiconductor, Power Integrations, Renesas Electronics, ROHM Semiconductor, Semtech, STMicroelectronics and Texas Instruments.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

Anyone can invest, but building a successful investment portfolio takes a combination of a few things: research, patience, and a little bit of risk. So, if you had invested in Monolithic Power a decade ago, you're probably feeling pretty good about your investment today.

Its expanding manufacturing capacity and diversified supply chain should help meet demand without a comparable rise in capital intensity. Higher operating leverage and ongoing cash generation reinforce the investment case. However, dependence on data-center spending, weaker notebook and consumer demand, rising input costs and a premium valuation remain risks. Intensifying competition, demand fluctuation and execution challenges could weigh on growth.

news.Title: Down from highs: Why GlobalFoundries is an essential chip play
news.Content:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Investing.com — Wall Street's semiconductor debate centers almost entirely on 2-nanometer and 3-nanometer processors built in Taiwan. Yet the modern economy—from connected automobiles and industrial robotics to aerospace communications and data center power grids—runs on mature specialty silicon, including 22nm and 12nm chips, FD-SOI, and silicon photonics.

Washington is increasingly treating this as a critical supply-chain vulnerability. With roughly 90% of advanced chip production concentrated in Taiwan through Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE:TSM), and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) burning billions in restructuring losses across its foundry division, reliable domestic manufacturing has become a geopolitical imperative. Despite that structural advantage, GlobalFoundries (NASDAQ:GFS) slipped 7.8% during the recent semiconductor pullback to trade near $38.62.

Spotting when an essential manufacturing bottleneck gets swept up in a broad sector pullback is what InvestingPro's ProPicks AI models look for. The system maintains GlobalFoundries inside the Tech Titans strategy's active November portfolio, where the specialty foundry is paired with a focused group of high-margin technology leaders—including an enterprise collaboration software platform, an essential semiconductor inspection monopoly, and a mission-critical cloud delivery network.

See the high-margin tech leaders in November's list: Explore the Tech Titans strategy on InvestingPro

The specialty silicon behind cars, radar and data centers

GlobalFoundries is the only scaled, pure-play specialty foundry operating manufacturing plants across the United States, Europe, and Singapore. Because its specialty chips are designed into products with multi-year lifecycles, the company benefits from highly visible, long-term supply agreements. Contracts with General Motors, Lockheed Martin, and Qualcomm underpin a multi-billion-dollar backlog across automotive radar, smart mobile devices, and aerospace systems. Further derisking its capital expenditures, the company secured $1.5 billion in direct U.S. CHIPS Act grants to support its domestic capacity expansion.

Recent third-quarter results demonstrated steady operational execution. Revenue reached $1.9 billion, up from $1.69 billion a year earlier, while operating income rose to $230 million from $195 million. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.53 beat consensus estimates by 3.9%.

AI data centers have emerged as the company's fastest-growing end market. In the second quarter, communications infrastructure and data center revenue jumped 62%, driven heavily by surging hyperscaler orders for silicon photonics and silicon germanium (SiGe) chips required for high-speed data transfer.

Story Continues

A share price that trails mature-node demand

Despite securing long-term government backing and expanding into data center architecture, the stock's valuation remains suppressed. Wall Street consensus estimates compiled on InvestingPro project 2026 EPS at $1.98 (pricing the stock at 19.5 times forward earnings), rising to $2.60 in 2027 and $3.52 in 2028—which would compress the multiple down to just 11.0 times.

InvestingPro's Fair Value models—which aggregate 12 independent valuation frameworks—benchmark the shares at $44.13, pointing to 14.3% upside from current trading levels. Analyst sentiment has been steadily improving, with 10 upward revisions to the current-quarter EPS estimate against just three downward revisions over the past 90 days. Across the 22 analysts covering the stock, the consensus price target stands at $64.77, offering substantial headroom.

The balance sheet provides a solid foundation for its capital-intensive roadmap, featuring approximately $2.26 billion in cash and short-term investments against just $1.72 billion in total debt. InvestingPro's Financial Health framework rates GlobalFoundries at "Fair Performance," with cash flow health ranking as its strongest pillar. Investors must weigh these strengths against near-term friction: the third quarter included a reported net loss of $271 million, while free cash flow temporarily contracted to $40 million from $406 million a year earlier as the company executed heavy facility investments.

Investors can evaluate the complete CHIPS Act funding timeline, the automotive order outlook, and detailed fab utilization rates inside the GlobalFoundries Pro Research Report.

Owning domestic chip supply without the AI premium

The race to 2-nanometer architecture will continue to dominate financial headlines, but the critical hardware inside defense systems, power grids, and connected vehicles requires reliable manufacturing close to home. GlobalFoundries provides exactly that infrastructure, yet the stock trades at a discount to its intrinsic Fair Value following a broader sector pullback.

news.Title: AI晶片股回神！韓日領軍反彈、台股祭限空令終結連七跌 市場緊盯CPI
news.Content:
亞洲股市周二(10日)延續全球科技股強勁反彈走勢，南韓與日本股市領漲，台股終結連七日跌勢。但由於輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳相關風波未明朗，加上美國通膨報告即將公布，投資人對這波反彈能否續航仍抱持審慎態度。

在華爾街創下約七個月來最大單日漲幅後，投資人正在重新買進先前遭重挫的晶片股。美國總統川普則釋出訊號，若與伊朗談判取得進展，美國不太可能再度發動攻擊，帶動油價進一步回落，緩解通膨疑慮也提振市場情緒。

MSCI亞太指數盤中上漲2%，南韓KOSPI指數大漲逾4%，日本日經225指數上漲超過2%，東證股價指數(TOPIX)上漲2.2%。

亞洲交易時段，那斯達克100期貨微跌不到0.1%，標普500期貨小漲0.15%。

韓股部分，SK海力士股價上漲6.3%，三星電子上漲4.9%。日股方面，鎧俠(Kioxia)上漲6.6%，TDK上漲5.2%，村田製作所上漲5.9%，LG Innotek上漲5.1%。

台灣加權指數盤中漲幅一度達6.4%，終場漲幅仍有2.5%。台積電(2330-TW)上漲2.2%，大立光(3008-TW)上漲2.8%，鴻海(2317-TW)上漲2.5%。

台股到周一為止已連七日下跌，創2022年以來最長連跌紀錄，周二終於止跌反彈。台灣金管會將放空額度上限從原本前30日平均成交量的30%調降至3%，並將最低融資保證金成數從90%提高至130%，同時維持最高新台幣5000億元(約152億美元)穩定市場基金可供運用。

日本與台灣股市上周均進入熊市，南韓股市則較夏季高點下跌逾40%，三星電子與SK海力士股價一度累計下跌逾16%。

美國10月消費者物價指數(CPI)將於周二公布，市場預期整體CPI與核心CPI將分別月增0.3%及0.2%。目前市場對聯準會(Fed)升息的預期機率已從一周前的74%升至84%。

另外，Anthropic周二可能展開的首次公開發行(IPO)投資人說明會，上市計畫，尋求最高693億美元估值，Anthropic上市計畫與本周稍晚的與CoreWeave(CRWV-US)財報，將成為觀察AI投資人意願的重要指標。

news.Title: 不演了？ 台股漲幅大收斂 他追旺宏、華邦電秒被套
news.Content:
台股今（10）日早盤跳空開高，盤中一度大漲逾1400點，不過隨著時間推移，漲勢一度逐漸收斂近千點，所幸在台積電由黑翻紅，也日月光、南亞、台達電重新鎖回漲停下，成功守住42000點大關。

台股上周歷經重挫回檔，指數一度摜破38000點，周一則迎來報復性反彈，今日則延續漲勢，早盤一度大漲逾1400點，雖然衝上43135點高點後一路下滑，漲勢收斂逾千點，但在觸及41930點後，在權值股集體拉抬下，指數又再度上揚400點，於42300點附近震盪；截至上午11:55點暫報42312點，上漲654點，漲幅1.57%。

權值股部分，台積電開高震盪，早盤衝上2280元後震盪走低，盤中甚至一度翻黑，但隨即又迅速翻紅成功，小漲5元，暫報2240元；台達電、南亞、日月光等權值股在大筆賣單下也一度漲停打開，不過後續又成功亮燈漲停。

針對今日的盤勢，有股民在臉書社團「當沖勒戒所」發文分享，早上看大漲於是衝進去買旺宏、華邦電，沒想到漲勢收斂，現賣現套「今天早上進場買旺宏、華邦電，馬上賠錢。」

留言區網友紛紛安慰，「平常心吧！很多人成交後，眼睜睜看著股價開始往下掉，笑你的人也發生過啦！」、「沒事的 當沖華邦電現在懊悔中」、「我買0050都能大賠了」；也有網友表示，「追高殺低才是真散戶」、「韭韭的」、「韭菜來了」。

（封面圖／東森新聞）

news.Title: 台積電營收出爐前...股價漲45元「市值重返59兆元大關」 1天增加一家南亞科
news.Content:
台積電（2330）10月營收於今（10）日下午出爐！在市場買盤與卡位資金強勢湧入下，台積電今日盤中強勢衝上 2,280元，上漲45元，漲幅超過2%，伴隨股價走揚，台積電整體市值也從 57.95 兆元直接衝上 59.11 兆元大關，光是單日市值就狂增逾1兆元，相當於一天拉出一整家南亞科的總市值，使市值重新站穩59兆元整數關卡。

資深台股分析師蔡明翰表示，輝達執行長黃仁勳陷入桃色風波，昨日輝達（Nvidia）釋出負面訊息引發修正，台積電今早表現卻展現極強韌性，雖然輝達與台積電連動度極高，致使昨日台積電 ADR 表現相對費城半導體指數略顯疲弱，但關鍵在於「該利空並未在整體半導體族群中擴散」，且費半指數終場仍強勢大漲。

蔡明翰指出，輝達昨日開低後並未一路下殺，反而出現強烈的開低拉回支撐，顯示市場對於10月至11月這波AI 族群大幅修正的「利空已出現鈍化現象」。當市場對利空不再過度恐慌，代表股市底部位階已經逐步確認，資金自然會重新回流核心績優股。因此只要輝達沒有發生實質性產業風暴，情緒未進一步惡化，這波大幅修正期已告一段落，對台股與台積電後市絕對是正面利多。

針對投資人的後續操作策略，蔡明翰提出兩大核心觀察點，第一，利空不跌即是底：市場目前已不再將輝達個案消息視為無差別利空解讀，AI 供應鏈最壞情況漸過，投資人毋須過度恐慌；第二，留意本周美股 CoreWeave 財報：身為 AI 算力基礎設施指標的 CoreWeave 即將公布財報，市場普遍預期其本業仍處虧損且資本支出龐大，若財報公布後市場能以「利空出盡」或理性態度消化，將進一步奠定AI族群築底反彈的堅實基礎。

news.Title: Will Cisco Systems (CSCO) Deliver the Strong Results the Market Needs to See?
news.Content:
With technology stocks recently coming under pressure amid concerns about lofty AI valuations, potential regulatory scrutiny, and immense infrastructure spending, Cisco Systems CSCO) will be among the most important AI-related companies reporting earnings this week.

While CSCO has not escaped the recent selloff, its strong year-to-date performance underscores investors' renewed enthusiasm for established networking and hardware companies.

Cisco's success highlights how the AI infrastructure buildout has revitalized longstanding technology leaders, including Dell Technologies DELL) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE), whose networking, servers, and computing hardware have become increasingly critical to AI data centers.

With Cisco scheduled to report its fiscal first-quarter results after market hours on Thursday, November 12, expectations are high for another strong quarter.

Cisco's Q1 Expectations

Cisco is expected to report Q1 adjusted earnings of $1.33 per share, representing 33% year-over-year growth from EPS of $1.00 in the prior-year quarter. This comes as Q1 revenue is projected to increase nearly 22% to $18.09 billion from $14.88 billion a year ago.

Momentum has been impressive, with Cisco's fiscal Q4 revenue rising 18% to $17.25 billion and adjusted EPS jumping 23% to $1.22.

More importantly, Cisco is benefiting from accelerating demand for AI networking infrastructure. The company secured $9.3 billion in AI infrastructure orders during fiscal 2026 and expects AI-related revenue from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in its current FY27, up from approximately $4 billion last year.

Investors will be closely watching whether this momentum can support another guidance increase, particularly as growing sales of lower-margin AI networking hardware could pressure overall gross margins.

CSCO Performance & Valuation Comparison

Despite the recent tech selloff, Cisco stock has still gained nearly 30% YTD, comfortably outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq's returns of just under 10%.

Over the last three years, CSCO has delivered a total return of more than 100% when including dividends, compared with roughly 80% for the broader indexes.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

At current levels of just under $100 a share, CSCO trades at 20X forward earnings, which is roughly on par with its Zacks Computer-Networking Industry average and near the S&P 500's 18X.

This suggests investors aren't paying an excessive premium for Cisco's expanding AI exposure, although its valuation is no longer as inexpensive as it was before the AI infrastructure spending boom. While CSCO trades above its decade-long median of 16X forward earnings, shares are still more than 35% below a high of 32X during this period.

Story Continues

Cisco's Generous Dividend

Intriguingly, Cisco offers a compelling income opportunity that remains relatively uncommon among major AI infrastructure beneficiaries and many tech stocks in general.

Its quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share equates to an annual payout of $1.68 and a yield approaching 2%, providing additional appeal for long-term investors.

Bottom Line: Can Cisco Keep Its Momentum?

Sporting a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , Cisco Systems remains an attractive way to capitalize on the AI infrastructure buildout without paying the premium valuations often associated with semiconductor and software stocks.

Strong quarterly results and upbeat guidance could reinforce confidence in Cisco's AI-driven growth trajectory while providing much-needed reassurance to investors following the broader tech selloff. However, sustained revenue growth and healthy margins will be essential to maintaining the stock's resilient momentum.

news.Title: Brave’s Leo assistant uses NEAR AI to prove its AI chats stay private, paving the way for businesses to use AI with sensitive data
news.Content:
Most of the AI tools businesses have adopted so far handle low-risk work, such as drafting emails, summarizing calls and cleaning up slide decks.

The material companies would most like to hand over is the material they guard most closely.

That includes financial research before it's published, legal files covered by attorney-client privilege and internal data on pricing, products and deals.

What holds that work back is usually not what the models can do. It's what happens to the data once it leaves the building.

Sending a confidential document to an AI model means trusting the cloud provider, the chip operator and the AI company not to see it. Most of the time, that trust rests on a privacy policy.

Related: Bernie Sanders spots opportunity as 66% of Americans oppose AI data centers

The pressure is showing up in corporate budgets. In Cisco's 2026 Data and Privacy Benchmark Study , 90% of the more than 5,200 IT and security professionals surveyed said their privacy programs have expanded because of AI. Cisco puts it plainly:

"AI ambition is outpacing readiness."

The cost of getting it wrong is rising too. IBM's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report puts the average breach at $4.99 million, a record. Attacks that pull sensitive data back out of AI models cost even more, at $6 million on average.

NEAR AI , the AI arm of the NEAR ecosystem, is building its business around replacing that policy with proof.

On October 15, the company announced that Leo, the AI assistant built into the Brave browser, now runs on private inference from NEAR AI Cloud.

Inference is the step where a model reads a prompt and produces an answer, and it's where user data is most exposed.

A locked room the operator can't enter

According to NEAR AI, Leo conversations on the GLM 5.3 Flash model run inside trusted execution environments, or TEEs.

A TEE is a walled-off section of a processor where code and data are shielded from the rest of the machine. NEAR AI says its TEEs are built on Intel TDX and NVIDIA Confidential Compute.

The company says the cloud host, the GPU operator and NEAR AI itself are "cryptographically locked out." Leo encrypts each prompt in the browser with a protocol called Oblivious HTTP, using a key that exists only inside the enclave.

Brave's relay strips the user's IP address before passing the request on. NEAR AI says memory stays encrypted while the model runs, and every response is signed inside the enclave.

The bigger point is who does the checking. Before Leo receives the enclave's key, Brave's own open-source verifier checks the hardware against Intel's signature and NVIDIA 's attestation service.

Story Continues

Attestation is a cryptographic proof of what hardware and software are running.

The verifier also rebuilds NEAR AI's code from public source to confirm it matches what is deployed. As the post puts it: "No pass, no key."

NEAR AI's Trust Center puts it in business terms. It says privacy is "enforced by hardware, not policy," and verifiable through attestation "checked against Intel and NVIDIA, not NEAR AI."

Trending on TheStreet Roundtable:

Veteran economist says investors are watching the wrong bubble

Billionaire Ray Dalio sounds alarm on AI's $4.4 trillion debt squeeze

Two big U.S.-listed Bitcoin miners plan major exit for AI

Brave's reach as a distribution channel

Distribution may matter as much as the technology. Privacy tools usually struggle because users have to go find them. Inside a browser, private inference becomes a setting.

Brave currently serves over 130 million monthly active users . That figure shows the size of the potential audience.

Private inference applies only to Brave Leo users who choose GLM 5.3 Flash in the model settings.

The rollout came in stages. Brave began testing NEAR AI's TEEs in November 2025 with DeepSeek V3.1 in Brave Nightly, its experimental build. The October release takes it to the full production browser.

Brendan Eich, co-founder and CEO of Brave, called the integration "a first for AI chats in browsers." Illia Polosukhin, co-founder of NEAR, framed it as a question of ownership.

"Browsers are a primary computing interface that handles all of our personal information, so it's critical that AI is introduced in a user-owned way," Polosukhin said.

NEAR AI says Brave joins Venice AI, Abound and the Government of Bermuda among organizations running production workloads on NEAR AI Cloud.

That mix of consumer apps and a public-sector user hints at the same distribution model at work: privacy delivered through software people already use, rather than a standalone product.

Guarantees that stop at the model

For businesses weighing sensitive workloads, the fine print matters. The privacy guarantee in the

Brave announcement covers one model in one deployment. NEAR AI describes GLM 5.3 Flash as an open-weights model under the MIT license, meaning its underlying parameters are public.

NEAR AI's Trust Center specifies that open-weight models hosted by NEAR AI run inside the TEEs. Third-party models are also offered, but NEAR AI says those are "proxied without revealing the customer's identity and processed under the provider's own data terms."

In other words, the hardware guarantee applies only where NEAR AI controls the hardware.

That distinction will likely shape how companies buy. A guarantee tied to a named model, a named deployment and an attestation anyone can check gives them something to audit.

NEAR AI also says a hardware-attested deployment log confirms that the model a user picks is the one answering.

Publishing open-source verification and relying on chipmakers' attestation services rather than its own word lets NEAR AI's approach be tested from outside.

For businesses that have kept their most sensitive files away from AI, that offers a way to bring them in without taking anyone's word for it.

Related: $13 trillion brokerage giant offers cheapest ways to trade crypto

Intel took 25 years to get back to its dot-com peak — and lost it in 6 months: Chart of the Day
news.Content:
Half off sounds like a deal. On Wall Street, it can be the start of a much bigger sale.

Right now, Intel ( INTC ), Arm ( ARM ), Sandisk ( SNDK ), and CoreWeave ( CRWV ) are among the AI darlings trading at less than half their 2026 highs, and chip stocks just lost nearly 30% in five weeks .

Chip stocks bounced Friday and roared back Monday. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) jumped about 7%, its best day since July, and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose more than 2%, its biggest gain since April.

Veteran trader Michael Martin isn't biting. "Lower prices mean lower market cap. It doesn't mean better value," said Martin, founder of TraderMindset.com, who works with Wall Street legend Victor "Trader Vic" Sperandeo .

"I keep hearing Gordon Gekko's voice in the back of my mind — 'A fool and their money are lucky to get together in the first place,' " he told Yahoo Finance.

His bigger worry is traders who talk themselves into holding on. "Don't confuse investor language with trader language," he said. "If you're a trader, be a trader."

Intel's long, strange trip

Martin's favorite example is Intel. "A lot of people think like, wow, Intel was 125. I can get it now for half that. It's a bargain," he said. "But at 55 or whatever it is, you can see 40 long before you're gonna see 140."

Intel's own history backs him up. The stock peaked at about $75 in August 2000, was down to half by October, and kept going, bottoming near $13 in 2002.

It didn't close above that dot-com peak again until April 24, 2026 . Loyal holders got a victory lap to about $141 in June before the AI selloff dragged the stock back below its old high on Oct. 30. Intel closed Monday at about $59, still up roughly 60% this year.

Intel had plenty of company. Five other dot-com leaders also kept falling after first being cut in half, from another 30% for Microsoft ( MSFT ) to another 88% for Amazon ( AMZN ), according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

None of that makes investor language wrong. Amazon now trades at nearly 50 times its 2000 peak.

But that's an investor's clock. Trouble starts when a trade gets judged on one.

How to keep a trade from becoming an accident

Martin, a discretionary trader for four decades, offers guidelines, not rules.

Size it small. If you're just scalping or trading a bounce, think $100 for every $100,000 in an account, or one-tenth of 1%.

Don't take losses home. "If you buy something on Tuesday … if it's showing a loss by Friday, it has to trade."

Know your clock. Younger investors "can buy quality names and hold them forever." Near retirement, "your first order of business here is to play superior defense."

Story Continues

When in doubt, sit it out. "Harvest some cash here and wait."

Martin's last guideline comes from hedge fund legend Paul Tudor Jones: risk $1 only where you see $5 or more of upside, a risk-reward ratio of at least 5-to-1. It "doesn't mean it's gonna show up," Martin said, but the payoff has to be there before you trade.

"You need to see massive amounts of asymmetry in this type of a market."

Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

news.Title: Why Marvell Technology Stock Fell Hard in October
news.Content:
Shares of Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), a semiconductor company , plunged last month as investors fled AI stocks on fears that tech companies are overspending on infrastructure. Shares declined further at the very end of the month after Bloomberg reported that Marvell would buy optical component maker Lumentum .

Marvell stock finished the month down 25.6%, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence . Here's what investors need to know about Marvell's unimpressive share price performance.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Marvell fell on AI spending fears and acquisition news

Marvell stock started the month strong after the company's management announced at its investor day that fiscal 2027 revenue would increase by 45% to $12 billion and 2028 sales would rise another 50% to $20 billion.

What's more, Marvell's leadership said revenue in 2031 would be $80 billion at the midpoint of guidance, nearly 10 times the company's fiscal 2026 sales.

But Marvell shareholders quickly forgot all of that good news as AI stocks declined during the month. Investors have become increasingly skeptical that the hundreds of billions of dollars technology companies are spending on AI data center infrastructure will be worth it.

Bank of America estimates that AI companies could double their spending by 2028, reaching $2.1 trillion. That's a hefty price tag, and investor fears are colliding with the fact that inflation is on the rise, causing many to worry that interest rate hikes could slow the economy and make borrowing even more expensive.

Finally, at the end of October, Bloomberg reported that Marvell was in advanced talks to purchase component maker Lumentum . Marvell will pay for the acquisition in an all-stock deal and values Lumentum at $115 billion. Investors were unhappy with the news because the purchase could significantly dilute existing shareholder value.

Marvell stock remains volatile

Marvell stock started November with a rapid decline, as investors continued to process the news of the Lumentum acquisition and remained concerned about AI spending in general. But Marvell's shares began rising again today as some tech investors rushed back into artificial intelligence stocks, believing that the sell-off over the past month is overdone.

Story Continues

All of which means that Marvell stock could remain volatile over the short term as shareholders try to determine if its recent acquisition -- which is expected to be completed in the first half of 2028 -- is the right move and if the broader AI trade will remain shaky.
