This observation leads to another fact: whenever the number of positive weekly candlesticks greatly outnumbers negative candlesticks over a rolling 10-week period, the historical tendency is for CSCO stock to rise higher than the random aggregate performance of any 10-week period (going back to the last five years).

Simply put, the observation of historical data suggests that there is typically a transition from an extremely bearish state to a future bullish state. In this particular circumstance — where Cisco stock has printed only three up weeks within a 10-week period — the probability of the ticker hitting the psychological target of $100 over the next five weeks is estimated at 46.7%.

From here, the narrative gets tricky.

CSCO Stock for the December Monthly Isn't a Good Deal

If we wanted to speculate on the above observation — that Cisco stock tends to transition from bearish to bullish states — the December monthly options chain (expiring Dec. 18) would presumably give us plenty of time. However, bull call spreads for that expiration period featuring a second-leg strike price of $100 only provide a maximum payout of 96.08% at time of writing.

Story Continues

From an expected value (EV) perspective, that's going to put our debit-based transaction into negative expectancy. I'm not saying that this idea is irrational as "rationality" is a philosophically relative term; what's rational to one person may be utterly bonkers to another. But if we both agree to use EV as a standard of rationality, then under that specific condition, the December monthly is not a good deal.

Shall we then extend the expiration date further out? That would lower time risk but would greatly escalate event risk — or the risk that plenty of stuff can happen between now and the January monthly chain. And because CSCO stock is such a stout investment overall, the market's expectation is for the security to recover by then. Subsequently, the payout for reaching $100 will be even lower, creating an even more negative expectancy.

It stinks but arguably, the more rational approach here is to consider the upcoming November monthly, which is only two weeks away. This reduces event risk (since there's less room for multiple variable events to materialize) at the expense of exponentially higher time risk.

However, the nuance here is the fiscal-first-quarter earnings disclosure scheduled for Nov. 12.

Is a Potential Upshot in the Works for Cisco Stock?

Right now, Barchart has the implied volatility (IV) for the November monthly chain at 73.41%. That's significant because the historical volatility reading for the period is only 38.92%. In other words, under baseline conditions, a standard bullish environment would likely have CSCO stock gradually drift higher. We're talking about a stock that features a 60-month beta of 1.01 — very much characteristic of a blue chip.

Obviously, anticipation is rising sharply ahead of the company's Q1 earnings report. Now, a high IV doesn't necessarily mean that CSCO stock will move northward; the volatility could just as easily send the ticker crashing down, particularly if results and/or guidance don't exceed the market's expectations.

Still, the contrarian viewpoint is as follows. Because Cisco stock has already incurred a heavy beatdown, it may only take a relatively small unit of good news to have a disproportionately positive impact on CSCO.

As for my personal speculation on the matter, I mentioned that Cisco's transitional dynamics lead to an estimated probability of 46.7% that CSCO stock will hit $100 over the next five weeks. It's possible, then, that this inferred move could occur over the next two weeks thanks to the potential earnings catalyst.

If you want to take a speculative shot, you may consider the 96/100 bull call spread expiring Nov. 20. With a maximum payout of 128.57% stemming from a $175 net debit, your EV would come out to $11.80 or a return on capital of +6.74%.

Granted, that's not the most attractive wager but it would keep you out of negative expectancy.

news.Title: Rambus (RMBS) Forms 'Hammer Chart Pattern': Time for Bottom Fishing?
news.Content:
Shares of Rambus (RMBS) have been struggling lately and have lost 12% over the past week. However, a hammer chart pattern was formed in its last trading session, which could mean that the stock found support with bulls being able to counteract the bears. So, it could witness a trend reversal down the road.

The formation of a hammer pattern is considered a technical indication of nearing a bottom with likely subsiding of selling pressure. But this is not the only factor that makes a bullish case for the stock. On the fundamental side, strong agreement among Wall Street analysts in raising earnings estimates for this memory chip designer enhances its prospects of a trend reversal.

Understanding Hammer Chart and the Technique to Trade It

This is one of the popular price patterns in candlestick charting. A minor difference between the opening and closing prices forms a small candle body, and a higher difference between the low of the day and the open or close forms a long lower wick (or vertical line). The length of the lower wick being at least twice the length of the real body, the candle resembles a 'hammer.'

In simple terms, during a downtrend, with bears having absolute control, a stock usually opens lower compared to the previous day's close, and again closes lower. On the day the hammer pattern is formed, maintaining the downtrend, the stock makes a new low. However, after eventually finding support at the low of the day, some amount of buying interest emerges, pushing the stock up to close the session near or slightly above its opening price.

When it occurs at the bottom of a downtrend, this pattern signals that the bears might have lost control over the price. And, the success of bulls in stopping the price from falling further indicates a potential trend reversal.

Hammer candles can occur on any timeframe -- such as one-minute, daily, weekly -- and are utilized by both short-term as well as long-term investors.

Like every technical indicator, the hammer chart pattern has its limitations. Particularly, as the strength of a hammer depends on its placement on the chart, it should always be used in conjunction with other bullish indicators.

Here's What Increases the Odds of a Turnaround for RMBS

An upward trend in earnings estimate revisions that RMBS has been witnessing lately can certainly be considered a bullish indicator on the fundamental side. That's because empirical research shows that trends in earnings estimate revisions are strongly correlated with near-term stock price movements.

Story Continues

The consensus EPS estimate for the current year has increased 4.8% over the last 30 days. This means that the Wall Street analysts covering RMBS are majorly in agreement about the company's potential to report better earnings than what they predicted earlier.

If this is not enough, you should note that RMBS currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. And stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #1 or 2 usually outperform the market. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Moreover, a Zacks Rank of 2 for Rambus is a more conclusive indication of a potential trend reversal, as the Zacks Rank has proven to be an excellent timing indicator that helps investors identify precisely when a company's prospects are beginning to improve.

news.Title: AAOI Stock Rises 7% Post Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold?
news.Content:
Applied Optoelectronics AAOI shares have risen 6.9% since it reported third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 5, 2026. The surge reflects robust demand for its data center and CATV products, driven by strong 400G and 800G transceiver shipments, AI infrastructure investments and increased sales of 1.8 GHz CATV amplifiers in the third quarter of 2026.

Click here to check the details of Applied Optoelectronics' third-quarter 2026 results.

Applied Optoelectronics stock has rallied 43.8% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's appreciation of 4.1% and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's decline of 2.9%.

The outperformance can be attributed to robust demand for AAOI's high-speed optical transceivers, driven by accelerating AI data-center investments. Rapid adoption of 400G and 800G products, expanding hyperscaler relationships, and a multiyear agreement for 1.6T transceivers further strengthened its growth prospects. The company is also benefiting from increased manufacturing capacity and improving profitability.

AAOI Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AAOI Benefits From AI-Led Optical Networking Demand

Applied Optoelectronics is benefiting from accelerating optical networking demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments and hyperscale data center upgrades. The growing adoption of 400G, 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers is strengthening Applied Optoelectronics' position in the data center market and supporting robust revenue growth.

In the third quarter of 2026, data center revenues increased 254% year over year and 45% sequentially to $155.6 million. Revenues from 800G products nearly quadrupled sequentially to $47.5 million, while 400G revenues nearly doubled to $93.4 million. This momentum highlights strong demand for advanced optical connectivity solutions supporting AI workloads.

The company's growth prospects received a boost from a multi-year agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale customer for 1.6T transceivers. AAOI expects this agreement to generate $1 billion to $1.5 billion in revenues through May 2029, subject to customer demand and supply conditions. The transition toward 1.6T products should support higher average selling prices and improved margins.

AAOI is aggressively expanding manufacturing capacity to capitalize on these opportunities. It expects monthly production capacity for 800G and 1.6T products to exceed one million units by the end of 2027. Growing opportunities in co-packaged optics and high-power lasers provide additional long-term growth avenues.

Story Continues

AAOI's Earnings Estimates Show Upward Trend

AAOI's robust demand for its next-generation data center products, particularly driven by the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and the company's continued product innovation, is expected to benefit the company's top-line growth.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Applied Optoelectronics expects revenues between $385 million and $420 million. Datacenter revenues are projected to be between $270 million and $300 million, while CATV revenues are expected to be between $105 million and $115 million.

Applied Optoelectronics expects non-GAAP earnings per share in the range of 48 cents to 63 cents. The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at 59 cents per share, unchanged over the past 30 days. The company reported a loss of 1 cent in the year-ago quarter.

AAOI Faces Margin Pressure and Rising Competition

Despite its expanding portfolio, Applied Optoelectronics faced margin pressure in the third quarter of 2026 due to an unfavorable product mix. Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 28.7% from 31% a year ago, falling below management's guidance of 29-30.5%. A faster-than-expected customer transition from 800G to 1.6T transceivers resulted in lower-than-anticipated 800G sales and a higher proportion of 400G products. 100G transceiver revenues also declined as a customer faced switch shortages linked to industry-wide memory supply constraints. Manufacturing capacity limitations and supply-chain bottlenecks also restricted the company's ability to fully capitalize on strong demand.

AAOI is also suffering from stiff competition from companies like Fabrinet FN, Lumentum LITE, and Coherent COHR, which are also expanding their footprint in the optical networking market.

Fabrinet is benefiting from strong demand for AI-driven data center infrastructure, particularly data center interconnect, optical transceivers, and high-performance computing. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Data center revenues jumped 78% year over year to $777 million. Data center revenues increased 16% sequentially and accounted for approximately 53% of total revenues.

Lumentum's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. In October 2026, Lumentum announced a collaboration with Astera Labs and Corning to demonstrate 1060 nm VCSEL-based PCIe-over-optics connectivity at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The technology aims to improve bandwidth density, power efficiency, and signal quality while addressing connectivity challenges in large-scale AI infrastructure

Coherent is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure spending, rising demand for 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, and growing adoption of optical connectivity across data centers. Rapid growth in its Scale Across business, the ramp-up of PhotonLink and optical circuit switches, and expanding indium phosphide manufacturing capacity are supporting revenue growth and margin expansion.

Applied Optoelectronics shares are also trading at a premium, as suggested by its Value Score of F.

What Should Investors Do With AAOI Stock?

Applied Optoelectronics' strong AI-driven optical networking demand, growing hyperscaler relationships and expanding manufacturing capacity support its long-term growth prospects.

Moreover, Wall Street's consensus price target implies roughly 211.19% upside from current levels.

However, margin pressure, supply-chain constraints and intense competition from companies like Fabrinet, Lumentum and Coherent remain headwinds.

Applied Optoelectronics currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting that it may be wise to wait for a more favorable entry point in the stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: LRCX Gains 8% on a $25B Buyback Plan: Is the Stock Worth Holding Now?
news.Content:
Lam Research Corporation LRCX shares rose 8.2% last Friday, following the company's announcement of a massive $25 billion share repurchase authorization on Nov. 5. The move offered some relief to investors after a difficult period for the semiconductor equipment maker.

Since reporting its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Oct. 21, Lam Research shares had come under heavy selling pressure, losing 23.1% amid concerns over its near-term outlook. For the second quarter, Lam Research expects revenues of $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million, non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5%, non-GAAP operating margin of 40.5% and non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) of $2.33, plus or minus 15 cents.

Although these projections indicate sequential growth and slightly higher margins, management acknowledged that supply-chain constraints would limit revenue potential. The outlook disappointed investors expecting stronger growth. The stock also came under pressure from a broader semiconductor sell-off, as macroeconomic uncertainties, profit-booking in AI infrastructure stocks and growing concerns over data center spending weighed on investor sentiment.

However, the latest capital return announcement has renewed some investor confidence. Lam Research's long-term business prospects remain encouraging, supported by rising AI-related chip demand and increasing semiconductor manufacturing complexity. Given its strong fundamentals and attractive long-term growth opportunities, investors should consider holding LRCX stock for now.

LRCX's Strong Q1 Performance Supports the Bullish Case

Lam Research delivered an impressive September quarter performance. Revenues increased 54% year over year to $8.22 billion compared with $5.32 billion in the year-ago quarter. Non-GAAP EPS surged 75% to $2.20 from $1.26.

Lam Research Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Lam Research Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Lam Research Corporation Quote

The company also reported a record non-GAAP gross margin of 52.4%, up from 50.6% in the prior-year quarter. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 40.2% from 35%. Operating margin crossed the 40% mark for the first time in the company's history.

Memory and foundry investments supported the strong performance. Memory accounted for 46% of systems revenues, with memory revenues increasing 120% year over year. NAND revenues rose approximately 40% sequentially, while foundry also delivered record revenues.

Lam Research's Customer Support Business Group ("CSBG") generated nearly $2.5 billion in revenues, increasing 40% year over year and marking its fourth consecutive quarterly record.

Story Continues

Robust AI Spending Supports LRCX's Long-Term Prospects

Lam Research's long-term growth prospects remain encouraging as AI adoption increases demand for advanced chips, memory and storage. Management expects worldwide wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending to reach the mid-$150 billion range in calendar year 2026, followed by more than $200 billion in 2027.

The company expects calendar year 2026 systems revenues to grow more than 40% year over year, marking its third consecutive year of outperforming the WFE market. Several technology trends support this outlook. Increasing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), advanced packaging, leading-edge foundry logic and next-generation NAND technologies is amplifying the need for sophisticated wafer fabrication equipment.

Lam Research is well-positioned to benefit from these developments through its deposition and etch technologies. Its Acara etch and Ether dry resist solutions are gaining traction in advanced chip manufacturing. Management now expects cumulative Ether-related revenues to reach approximately $2.5 billion by the end of this decade, around $1 billion above its previous expectation.

Lam Research expects its CSBG revenues to grow more than 15% year over year in calendar year 2027. This recurring service-related business provides an additional source of growth and helps reduce dependence on new equipment sales.

Management also believes the semiconductor industry is entering a multi-year investment cycle, with customer visibility extending through 2028.

LRCX's $25B Buyback Plan Strengthens Shareholder Returns

The latest capital return announcement provides another reason to remain invested in Lam Research. The $25 billion repurchase authorization supplements the remaining balance of approximately $3 billion from its previous authorization.

The company also declared a quarterly dividend of 33 cents per share, payable on Jan. 6, 2027. These initiatives reflect management's confidence in its cash generation and long-term business positioning.

Lam Research ended the September quarter with $7.45 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash compared with $5.60 billion in the June quarter. During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the company's free cash flow reached a record $3.24 billion. It repurchased shares worth $1.01 billion and paid $325 million in dividends during the quarter.

LRCX's Valuation Looks More Attractive After the Decline

Valuation also supports holding Lam Research shares. LRCX trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings multiple of 19.26, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector average of 16.79. However, the current multiple is significantly below its one-year median of 35.39 and close to its one-year low of 17.82.

Lam Research Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

This suggests that the recent correction has made the stock considerably more attractive from a valuation perspective. Given Lam Research's strong earnings growth, expanding margins and favorable industry outlook, its current valuation appears reasonable.

Compared with other semiconductor equipment makers, Lam Research trades at a lower multiple than ASML Holding ASML and KLA Corporation KLAC, while at a higher multiple than Applied Materials AMAT. At present, ASML Holding, KLA and Applied Materials trade at a forward 12-month P/E multiple of 23.64, 22.37 and 18.08, respectively.

Lam Research shares have outperformed the broader tech sector. LRCX stock has gained 17.1% year to date (YTD), significantly higher than the sector's 4.2% return. The stock has also surpassed the gains of KLA, but has underperformed ASML Holding and Applied Materials. Shares of ASML Holding, Applied Materials and KLA have soared 33.2%, 29.5% and 14%, respectively, YTD.

Lam Research YTD Price Return Performance

Conclusion: Hold Lam Research Stock for Now

Lam Research faces near-term challenges from supply-chain constraints and semiconductor market volatility. However, its record financial performance, strong AI-related growth opportunities, expanding service business and substantial shareholder return plans provide a solid long-term foundation. With its valuation also considerably lower than its 52-week average, investors should consider holding LRCX stock rather than selling into the recent weakness.

Lam Research currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Is Arm Stock a Buy on the Dip as Agentic AI Opportunity Emerges?
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM) shares continued their rollercoaster ride this year, sinking after its Q3 earnings report came out on Nov. 4. The semiconductor stock still trades up more than 50% on the year, although it's down more than 60% from its 52-week high.

The latest dip came despite management saying it is now more confident it can secure enough supply to hit $2 billion in central processing unit (CPU) revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028. With shipments set to begin later this calendar year, that is essentially five and a half fiscal quarters.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Arm has long used a licensing and subscription model, where it provides its IP (intellectual property) for customers to design their own chips. However, it surprised investors this year when it revealed that it would begin making its own chips for the first time, given the booming market in data center CPUs. At the time of the announcement, Arm projected that it would be able to take a 15% market share in what it saw becoming a $100 billion market by 2031. Since then, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices have projected that the market will reach $220 billion by 2030, given the surge in agentic AI.

Arm claims that its Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) CPUs provide twice the per-rack performance of AMD's EPYC 9755 CPU. Notably, though, this is a chip introduced in late 2024, not one of its newer chips based on AMD's new Venice architecture, which is designed specifically for agentic AI. Arm has orders for its AGI CPUs from multiple customers through calendar 2027, with shipments expected to begin in Q4 2026.

However, demand for its AGI CPUs isn't the big concern with investors; it's whether the company can produce its chips in a tight market for components and fab capacity. As such, the company's comments that it was becoming more comfortable reaching its loftier $2 billion CPU goal should be viewed as a positive.

Meanwhile, ARM said that its data center royalty revenue doubled in the quarter. It believes this revenue will continue to grow in the triple digits over the next few years as data centers transition from x86 architecture, used by AMD and Intel CPUs, to ARM-based solutions. It said it has a 50% server market share among large hyperscalers at the end of 2025, rising to 60% by the end of 2026.

Story Continues

Arm's core business, meanwhile, remained solid in fiscal Q2. Overall revenue climbed 27% to $1.44 billion, while annualized contract value (ACV), which smooths out license revenue, rose 12%. License revenue surged by 50% year over year to $773 million. The company said this was $100 million more than expected due to customers signing long-term deals to access its technology. It signed three new Arm Total Access agreements in the quarter, bringing the total to 60, and four compute subsystem licenses. Large shareholder and partner SoftBank contributed $209 million in revenue in the quarter.

Royalty revenue, meanwhile, rose by 8% year over year to $670 million. The growth was driven by continued adoption of its higher-cost Armv9 architecture and Arm CSS platform and growing data center business. This helped offset weakness in the smartphone market.

Looking ahead, Arm forecasts fiscal Q3 revenue to come in around $1.54 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 24%. License revenue is projected to surge roughly 50%, while royalty revenue is expected to rise in the low single digits given the pressures in the smartphone and PC markets due to high memory prices. It guided for adjusted earnings per share to be between $0.52 and $0.60.

Is Arm stock a buy?

Arm is well positioned to be one of the biggest beneficiaries of agentic AI through a combination of its booming custom CPU business and starting to sell its own server CPUs. The company projects it can generate around $2 billion in incremental revenue from its new AGI CPU business over the next five quarters starting in its fiscal Q4. Meanwhile, if it can achieve a 15% market share, that would grow to more than $30 billion in revenue for a market projected to hit $220 billion in a few years. This should more than overcome any weaknesses in current smartphones and PCs.

The question really comes down to valuation and growth. Arm has always commanded a huge multiple given its IP royalty and subscription business model, but now that it's designing its own chips, its multiple should shrink. Currently, the stock has a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of over 55 based on the fiscal 2028 (ending March 2028) consensus estimates. However, the longer-term consensus does not fully reflect the company's AGI CPU opportunity, with the fiscal 2031 analyst revenue estimate at just under $26 billion, though it could come in closer to $40 billion if things play out in its favor.

As such, I'd be a buyer of this AI stock on this recent dip, as it will likely look cheap in a few years if the AI build-out continues.

news.Title: Marvell Stock Fell 58% From Its Record. History Says What Followed Its Last 4 Drops This Deep.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) stock had a terrible start to November. On Nov. 2, shares dropped around 13% as the chip designer agreed to buy optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock deal.

The slide went on after the Nov. 3 elections sparked worries that new state limits might slow the building of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. On Nov. 5 alone, the stock lost 16%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

At its $133.55 close that day, Marvell sat about 58% off its record close of $316.43 on June 4.

A drop this deep isn't new to Marvell. Since its stock began trading in June 2000, it's fallen 55% or more from a record close four other times, going by split-adjusted daily closing prices. Twice, it needed over five years to get back to a record. The other two times, it was back at one within around three years of its high.

What type of drop is this one?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Two long waits

Marvell's first crash came during the dot-com bust. The stock sank around 92% from its Sept. 13, 2000, record close to its low on April 4, 2001.

And a 58% loss, which it hit in November 2000, was nowhere near the bottom. After that, shares dropped around 80% more.

The business wasn't the issue. Showing how fast Marvell was growing then, its revenue doubled to $288.8 million in the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2002, helped by its purchase of networking chip designer Galileo Technology. By fiscal 2006 (ended Jan. 28, 2006), revenue had hit around $1.7 billion. Even so, the stock didn't close at a new record until November 2005, over five years after its peak.

I'd say the 2000 share price had run so far ahead of the business that even growth like that needed years to catch up.

The second drop took much longer to make up. From a record close on Jan. 27, 2006, shares sank around 87% by Nov. 20, 2008, in the financial crisis. Once again, a 58% loss (hit in December 2007) came well before the bottom, with around 68% more to go.

This time, growth stalled. Marvell's revenue in fiscal 2009 (ended Jan. 31, 2009) came to around $2.95 billion. Twelve years later, fiscal 2021's total was around $2.97 billion. Not surprisingly, the stock went more than 14 years without a new record, finally beating its 2006 close in June 2020.

The last two crashes ended fast

Marvell's two latest drops played out very differently. Shares fell around 62% between Dec. 7, 2021, and Jan. 5, 2023, and around 61% between Jan. 23 and April 21, 2025. Each time, a 58% loss was close to the low -- shares fell only about 9% more in the first case and basically not at all in the second.

Story Continues

Revenue wasn't perfect in those years. Marvell's revenue climbed 33% in fiscal 2023 (ended Jan. 28, 2023), then slid around 7% the next year. But fiscal 2026 (ended Jan. 31, 2026), which included the April 2025 low, saw 42% growth to a record $8.2 billion, fueled by what management called robust AI demand.

And the stock followed. It closed at new records in November 2024 and April 2026, around two years and one year after each 58% mark.

Is Marvell stock a buy after this drop?

I think today's business looks far more like 2025 than 2008. Marvell's revenue growth is accelerating, from 28% year over year in fiscal 2027's first quarter to 37% in the second (ended Aug. 1).

On Nov. 2, the company said third-quarter revenue is tracking with its forecast of around $3.15 billion, which would mean growth of about 52%.

The price looks nothing like 2000's, either. At around $141, Marvell shares cost about 19 times the adjusted earnings expected from its own business in fiscal 2028 (the year ending in January 2028). At the June record, that same earnings estimate would put the price-to-earnings ratio near 43. In other words, investors today pay less than half as much as they did in June for the same expected profits.

Notably, the fall has mostly erased this year's rally, not years of gains. Marvell stock began 2026 around $85, so it's still up over 50% in 2026.

In the end, Marvell's history suggests the depth of a drop matters less than what revenue does next, and Marvell's revenue growth keeps speeding up. I think the stock is worth buying here.

Of course, a 58% loss was far from the bottom in two of the four past crashes, and the same might happen this time. That's why I'd space my purchases out over time.

news.Title: Arm and Qualcomm Lead Mobile Chip Design. 1 Stock Is the Better Buy.
news.Content:
The share prices of two mobile industry chip designers, Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM) and Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM), plummeted after they reported their quarterly earnings on Wednesday, Nov. 4.

Qualcomm stock was down roughly 14% after missing earnings estimates, while Arm stock also fell 14% on a weaker-than-hoped outlook. The lukewarm results happened to come out on a day when there was a massive post-election sell-off, with the Nasdaq Composite down roughly 1,000 points on Nov. 5, or about 4%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Is this a buying opportunity for either mobile chip provider ?

Arm stock has been a juggernaut

Qualcomm and Arm are market leaders in the industry, but they occupy different niches within the space. Qualcomm designs chips that are used in mobile phones and holds a market share of about 23%. It is second only to Taiwanese company MediaTek, which has a 31% share.

Arm designs the blueprints or architecture for mobile phone chips, which it licenses to companies like Qualcomm and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) that use the blueprints to design their chips. Arm has a massive 99% market share in mobile phone chip architecture. That moat is protected by the fact that Arm owns the intellectual property rights to the computer language and instructions that the chips use to run the mobile software. Competitors cannot build their own architecture to run apps without the language that Arm controls.

There has been a lot of legal back-and-forth between Qualcomm and Arm, with Arm suing Qualcomm in 2022 for trademark infringement over alleged use of its designs. Qualcomm then sued Arm in 2024 for violating its agreements by withholding support, among other charges. Last month, a jury voted in favor of Qualcomm with nominal damages awarded.

Since it went public in September 2023, Arm, based in the U.K., has been a juggernaut, fueled by its market dominance. It has posted an average annualized return of 47% over the past three years. Qualcomm has averaged a 9% return over the past three years.

The two stocks have been moving in different directions this year, with Arm stock up 55% year-to-date and Qualcomm stock down 8%. Will the latest earnings change the trajectory for one or the other?

Qualcomm stock is cheaper

Arm posted record revenue of $1.44 billion in its fiscal second quarter, which was up 27% year over year. Its licensing revenue jumped 50% to $773 million, while royalty revenue increased 8% to $670 million.

Story Continues

Adjusted net income was $566 million, or $0.52 per share, up from $0.39 in the same period a year ago. Both revenue and earnings beat analysts' consensus estimates.

For its Q3, Arm projects $1.54 billion in revenue and adjusted earnings of $0.56 per share. This beat consensus estimates of $1.53 billion in revenue and $0.55 per share in earnings. Shares were down on the slower, single-digit growth in royalty revenue and an outlook that perhaps didn't beat estimates by enough to satisfy its high P/E ratio of 220.

Qualcomm saw revenue decline 8% in the quarter to $10.44 billion, but that was higher than estimates of $10.12 billion. Adjusted earnings were down 28% year over year to $2.17 per share, which slightly beat estimates of $2.16 per share.

In its guidance for the current quarter, Qualcomm estimates revenue of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, which is higher at the midpoint than estimates of $10.48 billion. However, earnings are targeted at $2.15 and $2.35, which would be below consensus estimates of $2.27 per share.

Are either of these stocks a buy?

Of the two, Arm is in a much better position to grow long-term due to its dominance in the moblie industry, but also its growth in other markets, namely in AI data center chip design. But it is just way too expensive right now to consider.

Qualcomm is much cheaper, trading at 19 times earnings, but it faces headwinds with rising supply costs and that's putting a squeeze on earnings.

I wouldn't buy either right now, but you may want to revisit Arm stock after this sell-off to see if it settles at a more reasonable valuation.

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Bloom Energy, Skyworks Solutions and Quanta Services
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 9, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Bloom Energy BE, Skyworks Solutions SWKS, Quanta Services PWR and Micron Technology MU.

AI Stocks Plunge: Buy, Hold or Sell?

It has been a brutal week for some of the hottest stocks in the market, particularly those tied to artificial intelligence, semiconductors and the enormous infrastructure build-out supporting the industry.

On Thursday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged more than 12%, its second-worst day on record, while the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 dropped 4.4%. The selling was widespread, with some of the market's biggest winners suffering extraordinary one-day losses.

And all of this came just days after the midterm elections delivered a sweeping victory for Democrats, raising concerns about the future of AI infrastructure investment.

Today, technology and semiconductor stocks are bouncing sharply, offering some relief after the dramatic selloff. But investors are left with a difficult question: Is this an opportunity to buy the dip, or the beginning of the end for the AI bull market?

I certainly can't say for sure, but the evidence doesn't suggest the AI boom is over. In fact, I think there are some compelling opportunities emerging, though investors need to be selective.

Below, I will lay out the current setup and share why I think Bloom Energy , Skyworks Solutions and Quanta Services stand out.

What Really Caused the AI Stock Selloff?

The prevailing explanation for this week's selling is fairly straightforward. Democrats swept the midterm elections, the party is viewed as less friendly toward AI infrastructure development, and investors are suddenly concerned that tighter regulations could slow the build-out.

There is certainly some truth to that narrative. Opposition to data centers has been growing, particularly around electricity costs and the strain that new facilities place on local power systems.

However, I think the more important explanation is positioning.

The AI trade had become incredibly crowded, with enormous amounts of capital, much of it leveraged, concentrated in a relatively narrow group of companies.

When those positions begin moving against investors, selling can quickly become self-reinforcing. Losses force funds to reduce exposure, which drives prices lower and creates even more selling.

There is growing evidence that this is exactly what happened. Several hedge funds have suffered severe losses, with reports of managers cutting risk and reducing investment teams.

Story Continues

And importantly, the cracks were appearing well before the election.

Memory stocks began showing signs of weakness over the summer, while the Nasdaq had been gradually slipping since early October. The election may have been the catalyst that accelerated the selling, but I don't think it was the underlying cause.

Is the AI Bull Market Actually Over?

Despite the sharp deterioration in stock prices, I remain constructive on the broader outlook.

The economy continues to show considerable strength, and the bull market has been broadening beyond the handful of technology giants that initially drove the advance.

Meanwhile, the latest earnings season has been overwhelmingly positive. Earnings growth has been spreading across sectors, and corporate fundamentals generally remain healthy.

Most importantly, the AI infrastructure build-out continues to represent an enormous source of economic activity.

The hyperscalers have committed extraordinary sums of capital to data centers, semiconductors, networking equipment and electrical infrastructure. Current spending plans continue to point toward another substantial year of investment in 2027.

Of course, political risks shouldn't be dismissed. New restrictions on data center construction could delay projects and increase costs, particularly in states where opposition has intensified.

But I have a difficult time believing that Washington can simply bring this build-out to a halt. There are powerful economic and strategic incentives behind AI development, and plenty of states will welcome the investment, employment and tax revenue that comes with these projects.

The bigger risk, in my view, would be a meaningful deterioration in the economics of AI itself, followed by cuts to capital spending and earnings expectations.

So far, we haven't seen convincing evidence of that.

AI Stocks: Buy, Sell or Hold?

For investors who have held through this drawdown, I don't see a compelling reason to abandon fundamentally sound positions simply because prices have fallen sharply.

Selling after a violent deleveraging event is often a poor decision, particularly when the underlying earnings outlook remains intact. For investors who were underweight the sector or trimmed exposure during the rally, I think opportunities are beginning to emerge.

However, I am certainly not calling Thursday the bottom. Markets can remain volatile after this kind of liquidation, and some of the hardest-hit stocks may need considerable time to recover.

Micron Technology is a good example. While I remain constructive on the company's longer-term outlook, the stock has broken down from a large consolidation pattern. That is not the kind of technical setup I want to chase.

I would rather wait for Micron to establish a new base before considering an entry.

Instead, I'm looking for stocks with improving earnings estimates and technical setups that are holding up relatively well.

Bloom Energy Stock: A Direct Play on AI Power Demand

Bloom Energy manufactures fuel-cell systems that generate electricity on-site, allowing customers to secure power without relying entirely on the traditional electrical grid.

Its technology is particularly attractive to data centers, utilities and industrial customers that need substantial amounts of reliable electricity, often on accelerated timelines.

Energy has become one of the most important constraints on the AI infrastructure boom.

And I suspect an increasing share of data center electricity demand will need to be met through dedicated generation rather than simply adding more strain to public power systems. Bloom is one of the most direct ways to invest in that shift.

The fundamental outlook is exceptionally strong.

Bloom currently holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , with earnings estimates rising dramatically over the last month. Current quarter estimates have increased 39%, while full year estimates are up 23.3% and next-year estimates have risen 13.35%.

Revenue is projected to grow 125% this year and another 63% next year. Earnings growth is even more impressive, with expectations for increases of 338% and 70.9%, respectively.

At roughly 50x forward earnings, the valuation is certainly demanding, but I think the growth outlook goes a long way toward justifying that premium.

More importantly, the technical setup is attractive.

Following the recent selloff, Bloom has pulled back toward a key support level around $160, which has held so far.

That gives investors a relatively clear level to manage risk against. A sustained break below $160 would weaken the setup considerably, but as long as support holds, I think the risk/reward favors buyers.

Quanta Services Stock: The Infrastructure Builder

Quanta Services offers a somewhat different way to participate in the AI infrastructure boom.

The company is one of North America's largest specialty infrastructure contractors, building and maintaining electrical transmission lines, substations, grid connections and other essential power infrastructure.

And its business extends well beyond AI, with exposure to utilities, renewable energy, underground infrastructure and communications.

Whether electricity comes from the public grid or dedicated generation, somebody has to build the infrastructure required to deliver it. Quanta is exceptionally well positioned to benefit from that demand.

The numbers are impressive.

Quanta carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , with nearly unanimous upward earnings revisions. Current year estimates have increased 6.45%, while next year estimates are up 7.7%, including upgrades within the last week.

Revenue is expected to grow 43.4% this year and 18% next year, while earnings are projected to increase 62.7% and 18.4%, respectively.

Its latest quarterly results reinforced that momentum, with management reporting a record $63.7 billion backlog and raising its full-year outlook.

Shares trade around 29.1x forward earnings, which is not especially cheap, but reasonable considering the growth outlook and visibility into future demand.

Of the three stocks discussed here, Quanta may have the cleanest technical setup.

Shares have pulled back toward the bottom of a declining channel, creating an attractive potential entry point with a clearly defined risk level.

Skyworks Solutions Stock: A Semiconductor Recovery Play

Finally, Skyworks Solutions offers an opportunity that extends beyond the AI infrastructure trade.

Skyworks develops analog, radio-frequency and mixed-signal semiconductors used across smartphones, automotive systems, communications equipment and industrial applications.

The company recently completed its combination with Qorvo, creating a much larger semiconductor business with expanded exposure to defense, automotive, infrastructure and emerging physical AI applications.

I've been highlighting the developing recovery in analog semiconductors for the last couple of months.

Unlike some of the more speculative AI infrastructure names, analog chip companies benefit from a broader improvement in industrial activity and economic growth.

And that diversification is especially appealing in the current environment.

Skyworks also has some interesting AI-specific opportunities. In its November 3 earnings release, management highlighted new timing design wins in AI data center networking and the beginning of shipments of high-performance clocks for hyperscaler systems.

The company reported standalone quarterly revenue of $1.046 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.28 per share.

Meanwhile, earnings estimates have been moving higher, with unanimous upward revisions, including some within the last seven days. Shares currently carry a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) .

The combination of improving semiconductor demand, merger synergies and expanding exposure to AI infrastructure makes Skyworks an attractive way to participate in the next phase of the cycle without relying exclusively on hyperscaler capital spending.

What's Next for AI Stocks?

This week's selloff was extraordinary, but I don't see enough evidence to conclude that the underlying AI investment cycle has fundamentally changed.

However, I do think this correction raises an important question about what the next phase of the AI bull market might look like.

We are already roughly four years into this boom, and much of the early gains have been concentrated in the companies building the infrastructure behind AI. Those businesses should continue to benefit from substantial investment, but that doesn't necessarily mean they will remain the biggest winners in the stock market.

After all, AI is a paradigm-shifting technology that will eventually be integrated throughout virtually every corner of the economy. As adoption spreads, the investment opportunities are likely to evolve as well, potentially shifting toward the companies putting that infrastructure to productive use.

In other words, the stocks that led the market over the last several years may not be the same ones that lead over the next several.

I will be watching closely for signs of that transition, particularly in earnings estimates and the Zacks Rank. If revisions begin deteriorating across the infrastructure leaders while improving elsewhere, that could provide an early indication that market leadership is shifting.

For now, I remain constructive on the broader AI outlook and view this week's selling primarily as a positioning washout. But I also think investors need to remain flexible. The long-term opportunity is enormous, though the best way to participate in it through the stock market may look quite different in the years ahead.

中國股市A股三大指數周一（9日）收盤漲跌互見，國家統計局公布的數據顯示，10月消費者物價指數（CPI）較一年前上升0.7%。

上證指數周一收報3,660.79點，漲0.32%。深證成指收報11,145.49點，跌0.27%。創業板指收報2,458.56點，跌0.27%。

今年1～10月平均CPI比上年同期上漲0.9%。

與9月相比，10月CPI持平。其中，城市持平，農村下降0.1%；食品價格下降1.0%，非食品價格上漲0.2%；消費品價格下降0.1%，服務價格上漲0.1%。

10月生產者物價指數（全國工業生產者出廠價格，PPI）較去年同期上漲5.7%，較9月上漲0.7%。

工業生產者購進價格較一年前上漲7.9%，較9月上漲1.1%。

news.Title: 華邦電布局EUV，拚2030年導入
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-09 10:59:42 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電（2344）持續推進高雄廠擴建及製程升級，總經理陳沛銘(圖左)表示，14奈米製程將分為不使用及使用極紫外光（EUV）的兩代技術，若開發順利，預計2030年導入EUV。他也強調，日前通過的700多億元投資，涵蓋Module B土建、機電設施及部分長交期設備，正常交期的投資金會陸續加進來，因此該金額並非整個Module B的總投資金額，後續仍將依製程與設備需求分階段規劃。

陳沛銘指出，華邦電與ASML就EUV的合作已進行約三年半，目前派員赴ASML受訓、試跑及量測，為後續製程導入做準備。設備廠承諾予華邦首台EUV機台約兩年可以給，後續機台依現在交期要約三年半。隨著線路微縮，傳統多重曝光須反覆確保對位精準，EUV有助減少曝光步驟、縮短製程時間並改善良率。至於新廠設備配置，仍須考量16奈米與14奈米製程共用性、金屬層數等因素，現階段先安排交期較長的設備，整體配置仍有調整空間；建廠所需機電、配管及後續二次配工程人力短缺，也是擴產面臨的挑戰。

成熟規格記憶體方面，陳沛銘特別提及，今年公司車用產品的成長亦突出，車用記憶體約占全球記憶體市場3%至4%，隨國際大廠縮減DDR3、DDR4及LPDDR4供應，客戶積極尋求長期供貨，能見度因此特別提高。他特別指出，部分需求來自仍採用這些規格的新平台，並非僅為相容舊平台；過去須主動向客戶推廣，如今則有更多客戶上門洽談供應安排。

展望第四季，陳沛銘表示，記憶體價格仍將上漲，華邦電營收可望續增，但成長幅度將較前幾季縮小。終端市場方面，手機、PC及電視需求仍在修正，部分客戶透過調漲售價維持營業額，實際銷量及產能利用率卻降低，也有客戶調整記憶體配置以因應成本上升。他認為，延後的換機需求仍有回補可能，但後續走勢仍須觀察，不能將目前的漲價行情視為會持續向上。

news.Title: Buy the dip or wait? BofA maps out 3 scenarios for chip stocks and top picks
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Bank of America sees a potential recovery in semiconductor stocks in early 2027 as improving U.S. policy clarity, corporate buybacks and relatively attractive valuations help ease concerns over artificial intelligence spending, although investors may need to wait for earnings estimate cuts before the sector finds a durable bottom.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) has already fallen 37% from its recent peak, compared with an average correction of 32% during previous downturns. The bank said indiscriminate selling driven by fears of slowing AI capital expenditure could begin to run its course by early 2027, with congressional policy developments and share repurchases helping restore confidence.

Semiconductor stocks trade at 13.7 times forward earnings, a 22% discount to the S&P 500's 17.7 times multiple. A return to the historical trough valuation of around 12 times earnings would imply at most another 12% downside, according to BofA. The bank also highlighted buyback support from Lam Research, which has a $25 billion programme, ongoing repurchases by Nvidia and Micron's planned buyback start on December 9.

Previous semiconductor downturns suggest the sector typically declines six to nine months ahead of the fundamental earnings turn, before recovering as earnings estimate reductions become reflected in valuations. The SOX has gained an average of 42% during previous recoveries after those cuts were priced in.

BofA sees the late-June 2026 market peak as a potential signal that earnings estimate reductions could begin in the first quarter of 2027, as companies adjust second-half spending plans. However, the bank cautioned that cheaper valuations alone may not be sufficient to restore confidence, with actual earnings cuts likely needed to establish a sustainable floor.

AI spending remains the biggest swing factor

U.S. cloud capital expenditure is currently running at an annualised rate of about $1.2 trillion, with forecasts pointing to more than $1.5 trillion in 2027. If spending stabilises at current levels rather than accelerating, it would represent a roughly 20% downside against 2027 capital expenditure expectations.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

That scenario could reduce planned AI infrastructure deployment to around 30 gigawatts from more than 40 gigawatts in BofA's baseline assumptions. At an estimated $40 billion per gigawatt of investment, the adjustment could create substantial pressure on semiconductor revenue and earnings.

Story Continues

A 20% reduction in projected capital expenditure could translate into more than 20% lower sales and a 35% to 40% earnings-per-share headwind for AI-focused semiconductor companies. Nevertheless, BofA said spending reductions could disproportionately affect future land, power and data centre construction, while newer and more efficient chips, including Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, remain investment priorities.

BofA outlines three scenarios and top stock picks

Baseline case: The sector faces around 10% further downside before reaching a trough in the first quarter of 2027. The bank favours leading companies across computing, networking, semiconductor equipment, memory and analog chips. Its picks include Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Credo Technology, Marvell Technology, Astera Labs, Lam Research, KLA, Micron, Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and ON Semiconductor.

Bear case: A downturn extends into mid-2027 as AI capital expenditure weakens more decisively. Defensive companies, including electronic design automation providers Cadence Design Systems and Synopsys, high-free-cash-flow analog chipmakers Texas Instruments and Analog Devices, and less AI-exposed NXP Semiconductors, could outperform.

Bull case: A sharp recovery in AI investment drives stronger gains in higher-beta memory, optical networking, quantum computing and CPU stocks. BofA highlighted Micron, Credo Technology, Marvell Technology, AMD and Arm among potential beneficiaries.

Despite the recent selloff, BofA believes semiconductor valuations already reflect considerable scepticism about the AI investment cycle. The sector trades at a 22% discount to the broader market, compared with a 15% premium during the AI-driven rally. The key question for investors is whether earnings revisions and greater visibility on capital expenditure will provide the catalyst for a recovery, potentially shifting market attention towards a renewed AI spending cycle in 2028.

news.Title: Intel, Arm, and Marvell Have Each Been Cut in Half Since June. Only 1 Is a Stock I'd Buy Now.
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ:INTC), Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM), and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) all set record closes in June. Five months later, each stock is worth less than half as much.

Intel closed at $58.27 on Nov. 4, off around 59% from $140.94, its record close on June 22. Arm ended that day at $191.80, around 56% under its June 18 record close, and Marvell finished at $159.80, about 50% below where it closed on June 4.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

All three fell between around 4% and 7% on Nov. 4 alone, then slid further on Nov. 5. Investors were weighing whether Democrats' midterm wins might slow the build-out of artificial intelligence data centers, especially after Texas elected a governor who campaigned for a moratorium on new ones.

Falls this steep can make all three look like bargains. But each stock is still up over 40% in 2026. And only one of them expects its sales growth to keep speeding up, even as its stock got cheaper.

Marvell is that one, and it's the only one of the three I'd buy right now.

Image source: Getty Images.

Intel's PC problem

Intel's third quarter was strong, with revenue up 21% year over year. The problem is the outlook it gave on Oct. 29. Intel sees non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings of $0.25 per share for the fourth quarter, under half the $0.52 it earned in the third quarter.

PCs are the biggest reason. Higher memory prices have pushed up what new PCs cost, and Intel expects revenue in its PC chip segment to drop over 20% from the third quarter. Its chief financial officer, David Zinsner, sees the weakness lasting until at least mid-2027.

Yes, demand for Intel's server chips still tops what it can supply. But at around $54, Intel stock trades at around 36 times the earnings expected for 2026 and about 30 times the earnings expected for 2027.

Is Arm's royalty slowdown priced in?

Arm reported its fiscal 2027 second quarter (the three months ended Sept. 30) on the evening of Nov. 4. Revenue climbed 27% year over year to $1.44 billion, and its adjusted earnings per share increased 33% to $0.52.

The figure I'd follow most closely, though, is royalty revenue (the fees Arm gets for every Arm-based chip its partners ship). Royalties grew just 8% from a year earlier to $670 million, a sharp slowdown from 22% growth in fiscal Q1. Arm said memory prices hit the smartphone market and offset some of its gains elsewhere.

Story Continues

Licensing revenue, however, jumped 50% to $773 million, and management called licensing an important leading indicator of future royalty growth.

Sure, that might prove true. But at around $170, Arm stock trades at around 56 times its expected earnings for next fiscal year (ending March 2028). Even after a drop of around 60%, investors paying that price are arguably relying on royalties to speed up again soon.

Marvell's sales are speeding up

Marvell's numbers are going the other way. Its revenue growth has climbed each quarter of fiscal 2027 so far, from 28% year over year in the first quarter to 37% in the second (through Aug. 1). On Nov. 2, Marvell said fiscal third-quarter revenue is tracking with its $3.15 billion forecast, now within 2% either way. That'd be around 52% above the year-ago quarter. What's more, Marvell's August forecast called for $1.10 in adjusted earnings per share, up around 45% from $0.76 the year before.

The same day, Marvell agreed to buy optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) in an all-stock deal that values Lumentum at around $115 billion, including its debt. Lumentum shareholders would get 4.5 Marvell shares for every Lumentum share, leaving today's Marvell shareholders holding around two-thirds of the combined company. Closing is expected in the first half of 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approval.

At around $141, Marvell stock trades at around 19 times the earnings expected for fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028), based on Marvell's business alone.

Which one would I buy?

Intel's server chips and Arm's licensing business are each doing well. But Intel's profits are set to fall steeply this quarter, and Arm's royalty growth just slowed to 8%. At today's prices, I think both stocks still cost too much for these problems.

Marvell is the only one of the three whose latest forecast calls for its sales growth to speed up again. And based on next year's expected earnings, its price-to-earnings ratio is around a third of Arm's.

In the end, I think Marvell stock is worth buying here, maybe a bit at a time as the Lumentum deal moves toward closing.

news.Title: The 8x P/E AI Play: Why Silicon Motion (SIMO)’s Deep Discount Makes It a Strong Buy
news.Content:
We just published the list of 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires and Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ:SIMO) ranked 9th on the list.

In the first half of the year, memory was the hottest AI trade. Hyperscalers poured billions of dollars into data centers where high-bandwidth memory was one of the tightest bottlenecks in the supply chain. Most of the memory stocks rallied as a result, though the returns have been muted in the second half of the year so far, accompanied by high volatility.

Some on Wall Street say memory makers are sold out till 2030. Others say only till 2028. While the exact status of the industry can be debated, there's little doubt about the willingness of stock market investors to pay a higher multiple for memory stocks. This debate has been done to death, and memory makers continue to trade at extremely low forward earnings multiples, implying that the earnings cycle has peaked.

So what's the truth? Is it the end of the boom? Or is the structural shift in the memory business finally here? If you would rather avoid the high-risk nature of AI stocks, particularly memory and storage, you could look at companies that are doing the exact opposite, i.e., bringing in healthy cash flows and carrying low debt in our list of 10 Stocks With Low Debt and Strong Free Cash Flow .

But if you want exposure to the best memory stocks, read on. In my quest for the answer to the above questions, I reached out to a person who regularly interviews industry experts to find out answers to questions like these. I asked a famous Substack and X analyst, P Equity Research , whether 'this time was really different'. Here's what he had to say:

"There are essentially 3 important conditions these memory makers set in their LTAs: volume, price, duration. They are all negotiating LTAs to fix volume, a price floor, and duration of contract to get rid of past boom and bust cycles in the industry. As long as the Capex cycle holds strong, yes, they are sold out for 2028 and will be potentially beyond that."

So how are billionaire investors treating memory stocks with so much negativity surrounding the business? That's exactly what I wanted to find out with my article 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires.

Close-up of Silicon Die are being Extracted from Semiconductor Wafer and Attached to Substrate by Pick and Place Machine. Computer Chip Manufacturing at Fab. Semiconductor Packaging Process.

To come up with my article 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires, I first looked up multiple memory ETFs to list all memory stocks. In this list, I include stocks that derive at least 30% of their revenue from memory-related products and services. My list also bundles memory and storage stocks together. That is because some storage types also utilize memory chips and, more importantly, they face the exact same cyclicality that memory stocks are notorious for. They are listed in ascending order of the number of billionaires holding them in their portfolios.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation (NASDAQ: SIMO ) sits close to the memory makers without actually making memory. Its chips run the flash storage in SSDs and phones, so when memory demand rises or falls, Silicon Motion's sales tend to move in the same direction. High memory prices, which are a big reason that memory stocks have rallied so far this year, have also hurt Silicon Motion. Its phone storage chip sales fell 10% to 15% from the previous quarter, partly because phone makers are struggling to keep their devices affordable with memory this expensive.

Moving Beyond Smartphones

The company's overall performance has been strong, though. Last quarter, revenue jumped 131% to a record $560.2 million, beating the $529.1 million estimate. Earnings of $4.35 per share also came in well ahead of the $3.33 expected. The fastest growth came from storage products for cars and enterprise servers. That business has skyrocketed, growing about 27 times from a year ago and 75% from just the last quarter. During the same quarter last year, it made up 4% of total revenue. Now, that's grown to over 40%. It also recently finished designing a faster storage chip for AI data centers, and plans to send samples to the biggest cloud companies for testing in early 2027. If the tests go well, Silicon Motion could land some big orders. Management expects revenue to grow at least 40% in 2027.

Priced for a Downturn That Hasn't Arrived

Silicon Motion's stock looks cheap for a company growing this fast. At about 13x forward earnings, it trades roughly 32% below its 5-year average, while its price-to-sales ratio sits right in line with its history. When multiples are so low, it usually means that investors expect profits to shrink once the memory cycle cools. The balance sheet is decent. Silicon Motion carries $1.13 billion in debt against $846 million in cash. If demand from cars and AI keeps growing, I think this discount looks too steep.

Hedge fund interest has dropped, with the number of holders of Silicon Motion falling from 48 in Q1 to 34 in Q2. The value of their stakes also dropped from $901.7 million to $738.3 million.

Silicon Motion's sales still swing with the memory cycle, and its phone business shows how quickly high prices can hit demand. If that sort of volatility makes you uneasy, see our 10 Best Bear Market Stocks to Invest In Right Now for companies built to hold up even when markets turn rough.

news.Title: The Safest Way to Play the AI Memory Boom Without the Price Risk
news.Content:
We just published the list of 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires and Rambus Inc (NASDAQ:RMBS) ranked 8th on the list.

In the first half of the year, memory was the hottest AI trade. Hyperscalers poured billions of dollars into data centers where high-bandwidth memory was one of the tightest bottlenecks in the supply chain. Most of the memory stocks rallied as a result, though the returns have been muted in the second half of the year so far, accompanied by high volatility.

Some on Wall Street say memory makers are sold out till 2030. Others say only till 2028. While the exact status of the industry can be debated, there's little doubt about the willingness of stock market investors to pay a higher multiple for memory stocks. This debate has been done to death, and memory makers continue to trade at extremely low forward earnings multiples, implying that the earnings cycle has peaked.

So what's the truth? Is it the end of the boom? Or is the structural shift in the memory business finally here? If you would rather avoid the high-risk nature of AI stocks, particularly memory and storage, you could look at companies that are doing the exact opposite, i.e., bringing in healthy cash flows and carrying low debt in our list of 10 Stocks With Low Debt and Strong Free Cash Flow .

But if you want exposure to the best memory stocks, read on. In my quest for the answer to the above questions, I reached out to a person who regularly interviews industry experts to find out answers to questions like these. I asked a famous Substack and X analyst, P Equity Research , whether 'this time was really different'. Here's what he had to say:

"There are essentially 3 important conditions these memory makers set in their LTAs: volume, price, duration. They are all negotiating LTAs to fix volume, a price floor, and duration of contract to get rid of past boom and bust cycles in the industry. As long as the Capex cycle holds strong, yes, they are sold out for 2028 and will be potentially beyond that."

So how are billionaire investors treating memory stocks with so much negativity surrounding the business? That's exactly what I wanted to find out with my article 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires.

For illustration purposes only. Photo from Pixabay/Pexels

To come up with my article 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires, I first looked up multiple memory ETFs to list all memory stocks. In this list, I include stocks that derive at least 30% of their revenue from memory-related products and services. My list also bundles memory and storage stocks together. That is because some storage types also utilize memory chips and, more importantly, they face the exact same cyclicality that memory stocks are notorious for. They are listed in ascending order of the number of billionaires holding them in their portfolios.

Story Continues

Rambus Inc. (NASDAQ: RMBS ) sells its chips to the three big memory makers: Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix. These companies use Rambus' main chips, called RCDs, on the server memory modules they sell. The RCD sends the processor's instructions and timing signals to the memory chips so they run quickly and reliably. So the more AI data centers buy server memory, the more chips Rambus sells. One advantage it has over some of the names on our list is that it gets paid for each chip it ships, so a fall in memory prices hurts it less than it hurts the memory makers. It also earns royalties from its memory patents and sells chip designs to other chipmakers.

More Memory per Server, More Chips for Rambus

Last quarter, Rambus posted record revenue of $218.3 million, up 22% from a year ago and above its own guidance. Its chip sales reached $114.3 million, also a record. A big tailwind for Rambus is that new servers are moving from 8 memory channels to 12 or even 16. More channels means more memory modules per server, and each module needs these chips. So its chip sales could increase quite considerably. Its cash from operations also hit a record $102.5 million last quarter.

Steady Growth at a Fair Price

Rambus' valuation looks fair to me. At about 27x forward earnings, it trades slightly below its 5-year average, and its price-to-sales ratio sits in line with its history. What's different about Rambus from most memory stocks is how steady its growth outlook looks. Analysts expect earnings to grow around 25% a year for each of the next three years, which is a much smoother path than the boom-and-bust memory makers usually follow. If that holds, the P/E falls to about 14x by 2028. The balance sheet is clean. Rambus holds about $777 million in cash against $20 million in debt, making it essentially debt-free. For a company that benefits from the memory boom with less price risk, I think the multiples look pretty reasonable.

Hedge fund interest grew strongly, with the number holding Rambus climbing from 35 in Q1 to 50 in Q2. The value of their stakes also rose from $461.6 million to $848.0 million.

Stanley Druckenmiller made money for his investors every year for about 30 years straight, and Rambus is one of the AI stocks he owns. See which others made the cut in our 10 Best AI Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller .

news.Title: Here’s Why Lumentum (LITE) Was Downgraded
news.Content:
We just published a list of the Analysts Just Sounded the Alarm on These 10 Overhyped Stocks and Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) ranked 9th on this list.

Wall Street had a rough week, and the damage came fast. Thursday's sell-off erased $2.3 trillion in market value, pushed the Nasdaq into a correction and sent the VIX, the market's fear gauge, up 70% to 28, Yahoo Finance reported on November 6. A chip-sector index that plunged 12% on Thursday bounced 4% the next day, and oil fell below $100 a barrel.

Politics added to the swings. The Dow roared back on Wednesday after the midterm results removed election uncertainty, and oil fell on hopes of a deal with Iran, according to Yahoo Finance on November 5, though the rally was already cooling.

Interest rates became the bigger worry. Payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, far above the 65,000 economists expected, while unemployment slipped to 4.1% from 4.2%, Reuters reported on November 6.

Photo by Arturo Añez on Unsplash

Hot Jobs Data Raises the Odds of a Rate Hike

Traders read the numbers as a sign the Federal Reserve is not done tightening. Bets on a rate hike at the next meeting rose to 78% from 70% before the report, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.87%. The 30-year yield reached 5.27%.

Chief market economist Peter Cardillo said the labor market is at full employment and that the Fed has no choice but to raise rates in December. Chief investment strategist Susannah Streeter called the report hawkish and said she sees a couple of hikes before late next year, depending on the Iran conflict. Chief economic strategist Brian Jacobsen noted that wages rose 3.1% from a year earlier, yet real wages fell as inflation outpaced them, which he called the affordability crisis in one stat.

What Past Fear Spikes Have Meant for Stocks

Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi pointed to CBOE data showing eight earlier VIX jumps of this size since 1991. The S&P 500 gained an average of 3.0% one month later and 14.7% one year later. Our list of oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts are spotting 50%+ upside covers names that have been through a similar reset.

Hiring itself looks steady. Andy Challenger, who tracks corporate job cuts, called the current climate a "low-fire environment," with employers holding on to workers ahead of the holidays, according to Yahoo Finance on November 5.

Not everyone sees a hike as certain. Joe Saluzzi, co-head of equity trading at a New Jersey firm, called the jobs numbers very good but said the recent volatility could lead the Fed to hold off at its next meeting. Readers who follow the market's leaders can see our ranking of the best stocks near all-time highs according to Wall Street .

Story Continues

Lumentum has an average upside potential of 104%, based on analysts' average price target, and had 111 hedge fund holders in Q2 2026.

B. Riley downgraded Lumentum to Neutral from Buy on November 3 and set a $770 price target, down from $1,142, after Marvell's offer for the company. The offer was worth about $1,132 a share to Lumentum holders when announced.

The business behind it keeps growing. CEO Michael Hurlston told investors Lumentum landed its second major win in co-packaged and near-packaged optics, backed by purchase commitments of more than $5 billion. Those are orders customers have committed to before the parts ship, which gives the company a clear view of what it will sell.

Revenue rose 136.5% from a year earlier, led by pump lasers and optical circuit switches. The systems side of the business, which includes the switches, grew much faster than the components side. Hurlston expects about $350 million of added revenue in the fiscal second quarter, with profit margins widening again, and he sees optical switching growing into a multi-billion-dollar annual business. Marvell singled out Lumentum's laser designs and indium phosphide manufacturing as key additions. You might also be interested in reading our piece on whether Lumentum's valuation can hold up when it can't meet demand .

news.Title: Why Marvell Technology Stock Plunged 28.1% This Week
news.Content:
An agreement to acquire optical components provider Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) in an all-stock transaction valued at $115 billion sent Marvell Technology down 28.1% this week.

Marvell Technology stock changed hands at $141.20 as of the close on Friday, Nov. 6, having dropped 32% from Friday, Oct. 30's close, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence . Over the same period, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 2.7%, and the Nasdaq-100 was down 4.9%.

Image source: Getty Images.

A $115 billion optical deal sparks heavy dilution concerns

On Monday, Marvell disclosed an agreement to acquire Lumentum at an enterprise value of $115 billion. Under the terms of the all-stock deal, the buyer will issue 4.5 of its own shares for every Lumentum share outstanding. In an all-stock transaction, issuing new shares expands the total share count, diluting existing shareholders by reducing their percentage ownership of future earnings while handing a significant portion of the combined entity to the target owners. Wall Street reacted swiftly: analysts at Bank of America cut their rating to neutral, and TD Cowen downgraded the stock to hold, noting that $1 billion in projected annual cost cuts falls far short of offsetting a roughly 50% increase in share count.

Lumentum manufactures laser components and optical transceivers that convert light signals into electronic data inside high-speed networks. Combining those optical lasers with Marvell's electronic digital signal processors allows the buyer to offer integrated optical interconnect modules for data centers. However, regulators in China and the U.S. must approve the tie-up, a process management expects could stretch into early 2028. Analysts also warned that Lumentum competes with several of Marvell's existing chip customers, creating potential channel conflicts during the multi-year closing window.

Marvell Technology sells wired networking and data infrastructure chips that process and move data within data centers and telecommunications networks to cloud providers and equipment makers. While adding optical laser manufacturing expands the target market for artificial intelligence connectivity, paying a fivefold premium over Lumentum's share price from a year ago strains balance-sheet discipline. Marvell's $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum shifts the investment case from a high-margin data center chip growth story to a complex, dilutive integration bet with years of regulatory uncertainty.

What's next for Marvell Technology

Story Continues

Investors will get their next operational update when Marvell reports fiscal third-quarter results on Dec. 1, 2026. Management narrowed its preliminary quarterly revenue guidance to approximately $3.2 billion, but near-term financial results are taking a back seat to deal execution risks. The stock is down 57.2% (as of the close on Friday, Nov. 6) from its 52-week high of $329.88, reflecting how sharply sentiment turned following the merger news.

Marvell trades at a trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 52.6. Marvell's trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 46.5 sits in the middle of a wide peer group, including Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) at 37.5, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) at 96, and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) at 9.3, so the multiple on its own does not say whether the stock is cheap; execution on its core data center chip business does.

Is Marvell Technology stock a buy?

By uniting its strengths in electrical and optical interconnect with Lumentum's proficiency in high-performance lasers and optical transceivers, Marvell sees the acquisition as a major step in its drive to become a leader in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

The prospect of shareholder dilution from the acquisition and the current pushback from communities over the development of AI data centers, however, suggest that investors should be wary of the rosy picture Marvell's management is painting. As a result, investors with Marvell stock on their radars may want to continue watching from the sideline for the time being, waiting for the tech stock to dip further before considering a position.
